openalex.abstract: Traditional TCP congestion controls operate in a fully distributed, end-to-end manner. In the absence of explicit information about the network state, independently operating TCP flows must gradually and cautiously converge to high and fair rates. We propose Coordinated Congestion Control (C3), a hybrid congestion control approach that augments conventional end-to-end control with periodic guidance from a centralized reinforcement learning (RL) agent. Leveraging a global network view, C3 coordinates congestion window adjustments across flows, improving throughput, reducing latency, and accelerating convergence to fair throughput allocations. Our ns-3-based evaluations across diverse network scenarios show that C3-guided flows substantially improve latency and fairness over Cubic and BBRv1, while maintaining high throughput even under challenging conditions for congestion control, including reverse-path congestion and non-congestionrelated loss. Even infrequent C3 guidance already delivers significant performance gains.

openalex.abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the management challenges of transport networks for future Beyond 5G (B5G) and 6G systems. A novel management model based on the MPLS over QUIC (MOQUIC) concept is proposed, combining the benefits of Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) and the secure QUIC transport protocol. This solution provides end-to-end encryption, low latency, and efficient routing within heterogeneous environments integrating terrestrial (TN) and non-terrestrial (NTN) segments, including satellite systems, High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), optical links, and DOCSIS cable networks. The study focuses on calculating the probabilistic-temporal characteristics of MOQUIC tunnels. By analyzing packet behavior across sequential network nodes and accounting for burst concatenation and fragmentation effects, a mathematical queuing model is developed. Analytical expressions for average burst size and tunnel delay are derived, revealing a linear growth in burst size with an increasing number of nodes. The model is validated through discrete-event simulations, showing good agreement (relative error 5–15%). A practical applicability map in coordinates (tunnel length, load) is constructed, defining operational zones for URLLC, eMBB, and mMTC services. To enable real-time adaptive management, we propose a closed-loop control architecture integrating a hybrid prediction module (combining the analytical model with machine learning time-series forecasting) and a reinforcement learning (RL)-based decision engine. The RL agent dynamically selects optimal MPLS paths and QUIC parameters to guarantee service level agreements (SLAs). Simulation results demonstrate that the RL agent successfully learns to maintain URLLC delay constraints under varying network conditions. This work demonstrates the potential of combining probabilistic modeling with AI/ML to enhance the efficiency and reliability of B5G/6G transport infrastructure.

openalex.abstract: Modern communication networks are becoming more complex due to factors such as the rapid proliferation of varied devices, changing traffic patterns, and tight quality-of-service standards. It is challenging to respond in real time with rule-based or model-driven network management in such dynamic contexts. Cognitive networking holds great promise as it enables networks to see, understand, and adjust autonomously. This study presents a cognitive networking framework for optimising networks in real-time that is based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Intelligent and adaptive optimisation of routing, resource allocation, and congestion control is possible when network control is viewed as a sequential decision-making issue. By interacting with the network environment and learning the necessary rules from experience, the framework adapts to new scenarios without network models. The experimental results demonstrate that cognitive networking based on DRL outperforms typical optimisation methods in terms of latency, throughput, and packet loss, all while being scalable and stable.

Conventionalfixed-time traffic signals are incapable of adaptingto real-time traffic fluctuations, resulting inincreased waiting time, fuel consumption, trafficbottlenecks, and environmental pollution. Thisproject proposes an AI-powered adaptive trafficsignal control system that utilizes ArtificialIntelligence, Machine Learning, ReinforcementLearning, Computer Vision, and IoT technologiesto dynamically optimize traffic signal operationsbased on real-time traffic conditions. The proposedsystem continuously collects traffic informationusing CCTV cameras, IoT sensors, and connecteddevices to monitor vehicle density, queue length,pedestrian movement, and emergency vehiclepresence at intersections. Advanced deep learningalgorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs) and Reinforcement Learning modelsanalyze the collected data and automatically adjustsignal timing according to traffic demand. Thesystem also supports inter-intersectioncommunication, enabling synchronized traffic flowand reducing corridor-level congestion throughgreen-wave optimization. Emergency vehicles areprioritized through intelligent detection andautomated route clearance, improving emergencyresponse efficiency. The proposed frameworksignificantly reduces travel delay, trafficcongestion, idle time, fuel wastage, and vehicularemissions while improving road safety andcommuter experience. Additionally, the centralizedcloud-based monitoring dashboard allows trafficauthorities to analyze traffic patterns, visualizecongestion hotspots, and make data-drivendecisions for future urban planning. The systemcontributes to smart city development by providinga scalable, adaptive, sustainable, and intelligenttraffic management solution capable of handlingmodern urban mobility challenges effectively

openalex.abstract: General-Purpose Artificial Intelligence Systems (GPAIS), characterized by massive Foundation Models and dynamic Agentic workflows, impose infrastructure requirements that fundamentally contradict the original design principles of Cloud Native orchestration. While Kubernetes triumphed as the operating system for stateless, CPU-bound microservices, its legacy abstractions—specifically opaque resource counting and hardware-agnostic networking primitives—have proven insufficient for the bandwidth-critical demands of Large Scale Transformer training.This paper traces the architectural evolution of Kubernetes from a generic container orchestrator to a high-performance AI substrate. We analyze the transition from static provisioning to Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), which allows the scheduler to model complex hardware physics, specifically RoCE and InfiniBand fabric topologies. Building on the Kubernetes Network Driver (KND) model, we demonstrate how decoupling network plumbing from the orchestration layer enables direct hardware access (OS-bypass). This shift eliminates the kernel-processing overhead that historically plagued distributed training and allows for Rail-Optimized scheduling, ensuring that workloads align perfectly with the underlying dedicated network rails.We argue that this evolution is not merely an optimization but a necessity to support the next generation of GPAIS workloads—specifically the cyclical demands of Reinforcement Learning (RLHF). These workflows alternate between distinct phases with conflicting infrastructure needs: centralized high-throughput training (which demands strict RDMA rail alignment) and elastic inference (which prioritizes concurrency). We conclude by outlining the roadmap for a Topology-Aware Kubernetes that evolves from a passive provisioner into an active collaborator with higher-level runtime schedulers. By exposing fabric topologies through standard APIs, Kubernetes removes the friction of "Dual Scheduling," enabling application-level schedulers to request precise allocations while offloading the complexity of hardware configuration.

Offloading rendering tasks from resourceconstrained local devices to distributed computing clusters consisting of cloud and edge servers is a feasible solution. openalex.abstract: In complex communication scenarios, network capabilities are inherently constrained and reliability is frequently compromised, rendering existing infrastructures inadequate for diverse communication requirements. Consequently, constructing stable and dependable networks to ensure reliable transmission of mission-critical traffic has become imperative. Existing centralized traffic control mechanisms suffer from single-point vulnerabilities and prohibitive overhead, whereas purely distributed approaches fail to achieve globally optimal scheduling. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid traffic control architecture featuring centralized learning with distributed execution, and introduces a congestion control algorithm based on multi-agent deterministic policy gradient. The proposed architecture employs a multi-timescale hierarchical control paradigm, wherein the centralized SDN controller optimizes global routing strategies, while distributed intelligent network devices leverage the Actor-Critic framework to enable rapid local responses. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges rapidly to the optimal solution within 1,500 training episodes, exhibiting superior convergence speed and stability compared to both DDPG and QMIX baseline algorithms. In terms of network performance, the proposed method successfully postpones the first packet loss event to 50 seconds, achieving a 35% improvement over fixed service rate strategies. Moreover, when baseline algorithms experience packet loss, the maximum queue length of our method remains merely 20% of theirs, effectively mitigating network congestion. This study effectively resolves coordination and control challenges among distributed devices, significantly reduces packet loss rates, and substantially prolongs network lifetime.

openalex.abstract: Behavior trees (BTs) are widely used in game AI and robotics due to their modularity and interpretability. However, building them from scratch usually means heavy manual design and tedious debugging, which naturally inflates development costs. Reinforcement learning (RL), meanwhile, excels at discovering winning strategies automatically. The problem is that RL policies often act as “black boxes”—they lack interpretability and are highly difficult to edit or reuse directly. This paper proposes an automatic method for generating behavior trees from Q-learning. The method converts a learned policy into an executable and interpretable behavior tree, and further introduces a conservative subtree aggregation strategy to improve compactness and execution efficiency. Experiments were conducted in a custom game environment, where the game engine communicated with Python scripts via TCP. The result showed that the proposed method generates a more compact and interpretable behavior tree representation while preserving the correctness of the original policy and reducing the execution cost.

openalex.abstract: Microburst traffic in as often causes congestion misjudgment, buffer overflow, and challenges in space-ground coordination, severely threatening space missions. To address the above issues, a deep learning-based collaborative optimization method for TT&C microburst traffic is proposed. First, an ECN dynamic threshold optimization module is constructed, leveraging a lightweight fully connected network with LSTM and Transformer architectures, combined with reinforcement learning auxiliary mechanisms to dynamically perceive multidimensional features for adaptive threshold adjustment. Second, a PFC dual-threshold adaptive microburst recognition module is developed, featuring a three-layer architecture that integrates 1D CNN temporal feature extraction, attention mechanism-based key feature enhancement, and GNN network topology modeling to accurately identify microburst traffic. Third, a spatiotemporal compensation module combines GNN and LSTM fusion models to capture spatial and temporal characteristics of satellites and ground stations, improving delay prediction accuracy and ground station selection precision. Finally, a lightweight Actor network on onboard terminals extracts compressed features, while a central Critic network integrates these features with LSTM temporal modeling to achieve space-ground strategy coordination. Results demonstrate that this method outperforms traditional and single deep learning approaches in threshold optimization accuracy, microburst detection performance, and traffic collaborative optimization, significantly enhancing TT&C's capability to handle microburst traffic and providing robust technical support for stable space mission operations.

openalex.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents an effective clustering and routing framework for IoT cloud‐based wireless sensor networks using a newly proposed DRL‐dual‐conceptualized firefly weighted grey wolf optimization (DRL‐DCFF‐GWO) algorithm. The main goal of this work is to increase the throughput, the network lifetime, the routing reliability and the energy efficiency of large‐scale WSN systems while decreasing latency and packet congestion. This work proposes an integration of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and a metaheuristic combination of firefly algorithm (FA) weighting and grey wolf optimization (GWO) weighted by a cluster head choosing factor (CCF) to select the best cluster heads and the best routing paths at each sampling interval based on the online measurements of signal‐to‐interference‐and‐noise ratio (SINR), network congestion, and node survivability. Simulation results under NS‐2 demonstrate that the proposed DRL‐DCFF‐GWO significantly outperforms existing clustering and routing protocols, including chaotic GWO with slime mold algorithm (CGWOSMA), GWO–based sleep scheduling (GWOSS), low‐energy adaptive clustering hierarchy with ant colony optimization (LEACHACO), firefly algorithm based mobile sink routing (FIREFLYMS), and continuous particle swarm optimization (ContPSO). Specifically, the proposed DRL‐DCFF‐GWO achieves 8%–20% higher throughput, 10%–18% longer network lifetime, 12%–15% lower energy cost, and 10%–25% lower end‐to‐end delay than other techniques. The performance improvements indicated the effectiveness of the algorithm in minimizing energy consumption, reducing latency, and enhancing the reliability of data delivery over scalable IoT‐cloud WSN scenarios. DRL‐DCFF‐GWO can be used as a robust solution in various applications such as smart city monitoring, industrial IoT‐cloud applications such as smart cities and industrial IoT, environmental monitoring, and healthcare systems, providing flexible and efficient communication for the large‐scale deployment of WSNs.

openalex.abstract: In high-density cities, coordinating charging station (CS) real-time pricing to mitigate traffic congestion is considered a promising approach. However, the increasing complexity of transportation systems and multi-player dynamic interactions limit the effectiveness of existing pricing strategies in real-time congestion management. To address these, a real-time coordinated pricing framework for multiple CSs in coupled traffic-power networks based on Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulation is proposed in this paper. First, based on the established CS selection model for EVs, SUMO is utilized to simulate the real-time vehicle and road conditions of the transportation system under given charging prices, providing feedback on charging demand as well as individual and global traffic congestion costs. Next, an Adversarial Diverse Ensemble (ADE) surrogate-based traffic state prediction model is developed to overcome the time-intensive nature of SUMO and integrate it into the multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework. Then, a Graph Attention Network-based bi-level multi-agent Soft Actor-Critic (GAT-BLMASAC) algorithm is proposed to solve the coordinated pricing problem in a bi-level architecture, where the upper level optimizes bidding strategies of generation companies (GenCos) as price-makers and the lower level coordinates pricing among CSs as price-takers. Finally, simulations on a real-world Hong Kong transport network demonstrate that the pricing strategies derived from the proposed framework significantly mitigate traffic congestion while enhancing the total profit of CSs. The proposed algorithm exhibits robust convergence in the multi-leader-multi-follower game, offering a scalable solution for coordinated CS pricing in high-density urban settings.

openalex.display_name: Learning Selective Merge Policies for Deadline-Constrained Coded Caching via Deep Reinforcement Learning
openalex.abstract: In the coded caching, the server uses the cached information at the users to serve multiple users in parallel with a single coded multi-casting message or packet, that is, a merged packet, and thus mitigates the peak network congestion. In order to deliver the timely messages to the users in the deadline-driven applications like the video streaming, we must determine online the messages to be merged for the delivery, as there is a time limit for each request. It is important to note that while the merging aids the current coded multi-casting packet, it could harm the future deliveries. Our solution employs the deep reinforcement learning to view the coded multi-casting delivery as a masked action-discrete state control problem, and our policy network, trained via the proximal policy optimization, performs better than SACM++. On the uniform-demand benchmark, our policy network reduces the broadcast-packet expiration ratio $ρ$ by $40.9\%$ ($0.208$ vs.\ $0.352$) with respect to the best coded multi-casting baseline (SACM++), while also attaining the best broadcast-efficiency score $σ$ across the Track~A battery among the coded multi-casting methods. One noteworthy phenomenon here is that, for the applications with stricter deadlines, the merging becomes selective instead of aggressive, since the policy network selectively merges at approximately $31.8\%$ of the chances, even though the same observation holds across the variations within the same simulator family. The focus of our design is on the efficient pairwise XOR merging, where the higher-order ($K{\ge}3$) coding can be considered as a natural generalization left for future work.

openalex.abstract: The exponential growth of wireless communication services has intensified the demand for efficient spectrum utilization in fifth-generation (5G) networks. Conventional static spectrum assignment approaches exhibit significant limitations including bandwidth underutilization, network congestion, and inability to adapt to fluctuating traffic patterns. This research presents a comprehensive machine learning framework designed to address dynamic spectrum allocation challenges in 5G environments through intelligent prediction and real-time resource management. The proposed architecture integrates deep neural networks with reinforcement learning algorithms, specifically employing Long Short-Term Memory networks for temporal spectrum usage prediction and Deep Q-Networks for adaptive allocation optimization. Additionally, convolutional neural networks are incorporated to extract spatial-frequency features and detect interference patterns across the spectrum. Experimental evaluation conducted on realistic 5G network datasets demonstrates substantial performance improvements compared to traditional allocation methods. The framework achieves spectrum prediction accuracy of 96.2% while reducing handover latency by 37% and minimizing interference by 42%. Network throughput enhancement reaches 28% with a corresponding 19% reduction in packet loss for ultra-reliable low-latency communication applications. The system exhibits robust adaptability to varying network densities and traffic conditions, maintaining consistent quality of service across heterogeneous deployment scenarios. Federated learning integration enables privacy-preserving collaborative optimization across multiple base stations. These findings confirm that machine learning-driven dynamic spectrum allocation provides a viable path toward self-optimizing, high-performance wireless networks capable of meeting the diverse requirements of next-generation communication systems including enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine-type communications, and mission-critical services.

openalex.abstract: Recent advances have sparked growing interest in applying pre-trained large language models (LLMs) to time series forecasting. However, three major challenges remain: (1) achieving robust generalization across domains, (2) aligning heterogeneous temporal and textual modalities, and (3) mitigating cumulative prediction errors in autoregressive settings. To tackle these issues, we propose LangTime, a unified, language-guided framework that integrates cross-domain pre-training with reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning. LangTime introduces Temporal Comprehension Prompts (TCPs)—dataset- and channel-aware instructions that enable domain adaptation and compress temporal dynamics into a single token, enhancing the LLM's ability to interpret and align time series data. To further stabilize autoregressive predictions, we develop TimePPO, a reinforcement learning fine-tuning algorithm that reduces error propagation through a multidimensional reward formulation and a repetition-based value estimation mechanism. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that LangTime achieves superior cross-domain forecasting accuracy, while TimePPO substantially improves the robustness and precision of autoregressive modeling.

openalex.abstract: Network measurement is now a basic building block that supports network management applications to identify real-time events by measuring both large and small flows. However, existing techniques face the trade-off between high accuracy and resource efficiency: sketch-based techniques enjoy high accuracy and low resource consumption when measuring large flows but drop accuracy for small flows; in-band network telemetry (INT) measures every flow at the cost of high resource consumption. In this paper, we present MonPlan, a framework that utilizes both sketches and INT to measure large and small flows, respectively, offering both high measurement accuracy and resource efficiency. Unlike existing studies, our co-design is driven by two theoretical optimizations: (1) MonPlan adopts the near-optimal Lagrangian relaxation to solve the NP-hard selection of measurement points to deploy sketches and INT even when the routing information is unknown. (2) MonPlan estimates the worst-case rates of collecting measurement data. Its estimates support reinforcement learning to select paths without network congestions. We realize MonPlan on 12.8 Tbps programmable switches. With large-scale real-world topologies and nine network management applications, MonPlan provides 23∼95% higher accuracy and retains resource efficiency when compared with five types of existing techniques.

openalex.display_name: Fair-Aurora: Comparing Fairness Strategies for Reinforcement Learning-Based Congestion Control in Multi-Flow Environments
openalex.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for Internet congestion control, achieving higher link utilization than classical heuristics. However, RL-based controllers trained in single-flow environments are not guaranteed to share bandwidth equitably when deployed in multi-flow networks. This paper investigates the fairness properties of Aurora~\cite{jay2019aurora}, a state-of-the-art deep RL congestion controller, and evaluates three post-hoc fairness strategies that preserve Aurora's RL architecture: \emph{reward shaping} (Strategy~A), \emph{observation augmentation} (Strategy~B), and \emph{loss-sensitivity tuning} (Strategy~C). Using a custom shared-bottleneck simulator and Jain's fairness index as the primary metric, we find that modest reward shaping achieves the best fairness while preserving aggregate throughput. All strategies maintain the total bandwidth budget with fairness being achieved through redistribution, not reduction. Beyond the 2-flow homogeneous setting, an extended evaluation across mixed Aurora--CUBIC competition and dynamic flow entry/exit scenarios shows that Strategy~C's loss-sensitivity emerges as the most TCP-friendly mechanism, while Strategy~B is the most stable through dynamic flow-set changes.

openalex.abstract: Congestion controllers (CCs) are critical to network performance, and yet their robustness under adverse conditions remains insufficiently understood. While recent learning-based CCs have demonstrated strong performance in controlled environments, it is unclear how they compare to traditional CCs when controllers' input signals are corrupted or when environmental conditions become systematically challenging. In this paper, we introduce CCLab, an adversarial testing framework for systematically evaluating the robustness of both learning-based and non-learning-based CCs. CCLab includes a reinforcement learning (RL)-based adversarial agent that operates in a closed loop with the congestion control policy, generating bounded perturbations either on input signals (feature-level) or on external network conditions (environment-level), while preserving realism through explicit constraints. Using this framework, we compare learning-based CCs with non-learning-based CCs under both feature-level and environment-level adversarial conditions. While both types of CCs suffer from performance degradation under adversarial testing, we find that learning-based CCs, in general, are more robust than traditional human-designed algorithms. Finally, we show that our adversarial traces can be used to train more robust CCs that outperform existing learning-based CCs under both challenging and normal conditions.

openalex.abstract: Accurate bandwidth estimation is crucial for optimizing quality of experience (QoE) in real-time communication (RTC) systems. While online reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise in adapting to dynamic networks, it suffers from instability, exploration risk, and high deployment cost. Offline RL mitigates these issues by learning from pre-collected trajectories, but existing methods often rely on simplistic architectures and lack efficient policy modeling. openalex.abstract: Persistent Memory (PM) and Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) technologies have significantly improved the storage and network performance in data centers and spawned a slew of distributed file systems (DFS) designs. Existing DFSs often consider remote storage a performance constraint, assuming it delivers lower bandwidth and higher latency than local devices. However, the advancements in RDMA technology present an opportunity to narrow the performance disparity between local and remote access, empowering DFSs to harness both local and remote I/O capabilities, thereby attaining higher aggregated throughput. We propose SwitchFS, a new DFS architecture that exploits all the available PM bandwidth in a cluster with generative I/O path assignment policy. It dynamically steers client-side I/O requests to the local cache and the remote devices accessible through RDMA network. To determine the run-time I/O path adaptively, we introduce MELON, an I/O path selection policy based on a reinforcement learning model, designed to optimize expected I/O latency. Meanwhile, SwitchFS adopts a model-driven opportunistic replication mechanism at the server-side, which further improves I/O bandwidth utilization of remote devices across the cluster. Furthermore, we adopt the fine-grained concurrency control approach to improve scalability. Across synthetic and real-world application workloads, SwitchFS improves throughput by up to 5.9× over existing DFS designs while preserving low tail latency and incurring modest learning overhead.

openalex.abstract: Overview This repository contains the official dataset, deployment telemetry, and explainable AI (XAI) incident logs for the GRAD-RL (Graph-Informed Autonomous Cyber-Physical Defense) framework. The dataset is generated and evaluated within the GRFICSv3 industrial control system (ICS) environment and is explicitly annotated with MITRE ATT&CK for ICS techniques. This dataset is designed to evaluate multi-stage autonomous defense mechanisms, anomaly detection algorithms, and safety-constrained reinforcement learning agents in critical infrastructure settings. File Structure & Data Dictionary 1. grad_rl_final_dataset.csv (Main Dataset) Contains 90,728 samples of multivariate time-series data captured from the ICS environment during normal operations and active cyberattacks. Network & Physical Features: Continuous sensor readings (e.g., flow rates, pressure levels), actuator states (valves, pumps), and network telemetry (Modbus/TCP traffic metadata). Label: Binary classification target (0 = Normal, 1 = Attack). MITRE_Technique: Granular MITRE ATT&CK for ICS annotations (e.g., T0836 - Modification of Parameter, T0856 - Spoofing Standard Network Operating Data). 2. telemetry_audit.csv (Live Deployment Log) The operational telemetry recorded during the live deployment of the GRAD-RL framework. It logs the continuous interactions between the PPO RL agent and the deterministic safety gate. Timestamp: Execution timestamp (ms resolution). Risk_Score: The continuous risk tensor output (0.0 to 10.0) calculated via graph centrality and CVSS v4.0 impact vectors. RL_Action: The autonomous mitigation action proposed by the PPO agent (e.g., ISOLATE_ZONE, BLOCK_IP). Gate_Decision: The final safety-constrained action enforced by the IEC 61511 safety gate (e.g., REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL). 3. xai_incidents.json (Explainable AI Records) Structured JSON records generated by the Detective Node's XGBoost classifier, providing interpretable incident reports for human operators. Incident_ID: Unique identifier for the detected anomaly window. Attack_Class: The predicted attack family. Culprit_Features: The top features (sensors/actuators) that contributed to the anomaly, based on SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values. 4. experiment_journal.txt (Ground Truth & Timeline) A chronological journal detailing the experimental setup, attack execution windows, and ground truth timestamps. Essential for aligning the telemetry logs with the physical attack scenarios. Usage & License This dataset is released under the CC BY 4.0 License. You are free to share and adapt the material for any purpose, even commercially, provided you give appropriate credit to the original authors. For the associated source code, reinforcement learning models, and training pipelines, please refer to the official GitHub repository linked in the metadata.

openalex.abstract: Integrating green hydrogen systems into hybrid microgrids introduces nonlinear dynamics that compromise control stability during operational transitions. The performance of the advanced control loops depends on the latency and reliability provided by the communication infrastructure. This paper proposes a Software-Defined Networking (SDN) architecture integrated with an adaptive Quality of Service (AQoS) framework to support time-critical data flows in a hybrid microgrid with green hydrogen integration. An emulated network topology in GNS3, with OpenDaylight as the SDN controller and Open vSwitch as the forwarding plane, reproduces IEC 61850 traffic patterns, including GOOSE, control set-points and MMS. These traffic classes coordinate key microgrid components, including electrolysers, fuel cells and battery storage. Experimental results show that the SDN-AQoS framework reduces latency variance by 60% compared to unmanaged SDN configurations and delivers 49.4% higher throughput than traditional TCP/IP networks under congestion. The SDN-AQoS configuration achieves a median latency of 9.68 ms, keeping 97.5% of the measurements below the 20 ms safety threshold for electrolyser control. This level of reliability represents a substantial improvement over the plain TCP/IP at 90%, unmanaged SDN at 66.7% and static QoS policing at 60%. QoS rules are configured through the RESTCONF interface and remain fixed during each experiment while enabling the future integration of reinforcement learning agents for autonomous QoS adaptation. At the same time, this framework supports the bounded communication delay required to sustain frequency control and electrolyser safety coordination in low-inertia hydrogen microgrids during network congestion. The physical layer impact of these communication improvements remains a subject of future hardware-in-the-loop validation.

openalex.abstract: Urban traffic congestion poses a persistent challenge to modern cities, resulting in increased travel delay, energy consumption, and economic loss. As a critical problem in intelligent transportation systems, urban congestion management requires coordinated and adaptive decision-making across both supply-side and demand-side control mechanisms. Existing traffic management approaches usually address congestion from either the supply side through traffic signal control or the demand side via congestion pricing, while their intrinsic interactions and multi-scale coordination remain insufficiently explored. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework, termed JCPO-DRL, for joint congestion and pricing optimization in urban traffic networks. The framework decomposes the joint control task into a two-layer decision process, where an upper-layer policy regulates network-level congestion pricing at a coarse temporal scale and a lower-layer policy performs adaptive traffic signal control conditioned on pricing decisions, enabling coordinated supply–demand regulation while avoiding the curse of dimensionality. Extensive experiments under diverse traffic scenarios show that JCPO-DRL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art signal-only and pricing-only baselines, reducing average travel delay by up to 19% and improving traffic throughput by up to 4% compared with representative baselines, and maintaining moderate congestion pricing cost. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of hierarchical joint optimization and highlight the potential of the proposed framework for intelligent urban traffic management in intelligent transportation systems.

openalex.abstract: The proliferation of 6G networks poses new challenges to traditional methods of network management due to the massive volumes of data generated and the wide variety of devices they link. A paradigm change towards AI frameworks built in Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) is essential due to the shortcomings of these approaches. A Speed-optimized Attention-based Hybrid Graph Convolutional Network-Long Short-Term Memory (SPAH-GCN-LSTM) model and a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework utilizing Q-Learning (QL) were developed to forecast network congestion and enhance data transmission routes, respectively. Nevertheless, in a dynamic network, uncertainty in routing decisions could be caused by the switching between policies by a single agent. The time spent training one agent is prohibitive with the increase of the size of the network. In spite of the fact that multi-agent RLhas been utilized to alleviate this problem, classical QL can potentially face the challenge of non-stationarity that arises because of the joint learning of other agents in a multi-agent stochastic-game environment. As a result, the present manuscript presents a Multi-Agent Multi-Step Deep QL(MAMS-DQL) system that is aimed at optimizing Washington routes in 6G networks. The main goal is to come up with a decentralized mechanism where every agent is able to choose its best routing strategy independently. The multi-agent dueling deep Q-network architecture is followed in this method so as to optimize routing decisions and identify the most efficient route of the network. It also uses a multi-step experience-replay strategy, which allows agents to modify their routing strategy by taking advantage of multi-step experiences across consecutive time steps of training. Lastly, the outcomes of the simulator show that the MAMS-DQL has a higher routing efficiency compared to traditional reinforcement-learning approaches.

openalex.abstract: Software Defined Networking (SDN) has become the main factor in providing architectures that can be scalable and flexible in 5G as well as Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) environments. In distributed SDN control planes, load balancing among the controllers is very important to maintain the low latency values needed by delay-sensitive applications. The solutions currently in use are mostly reactive, where the switch migrations are only initiated after the occurrence of overloads or pre-emptive, which depend on forecasts that can be incorrect due to sudden traffic changes. In this paper, the authors have presented an online learning-based load balancing framework which not only adjusts the controller assignments without any long-term predictions but can also adaptively modify the load. In particular, as an illustration of equally exploring and exploiting the solutions of the different bandit problems, the application of multi-armed bandit and online convex optimization algorithms to face the challenge of sublinear regret when selecting migration actions has been considered. Extensive simulations on Mininet with realistic TCP, UDP, VoIP, and HTTP traffic reduces controller delay imbalance by$\mathbf{1 5}-\mathbf{2 5 \%}$compared to baselines, lowers migration cost by$20-30 \%$, ensures VoIP and gaming latency$<80 \text{ms}$, sustaining stringent QoS requirements, and achieves nearoptimal performance across$\mathbf{1 0, 0 0 0}$simulation rounds. The results back the claim that it is a practical solution for delaysensitive SDN deployment scenarios at the network edge.

openalex.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown remarkable performance on complex control problems in systems and networking, including adaptive video streaming, wireless resource management, and congestion control. For safe deployment, however, it is critical to reason about how agents behave across the range of system states they may encounter in practice. Existing verification-based approaches in this domain primarily focus on point properties -- properties defined around fixed input states -- which offer limited coverage and require substantial manual effort to identify relevant input-output pairs for analysis. In this paper, we study symbolic properties -- properties that specify expected behaviors over ranges of input states -- for DRL agents in systems and networking. We present a generic formulation for symbolic properties, with monotonicity and robustness as concrete examples, and show how they can be analyzed using existing DNN verification engines. Our approach encodes symbolic properties as comparisons between related executions of the same policy and decomposes them into practically tractable sub-properties. These techniques serve as practical enablers for applying existing verification tools to symbolic analysis. Using our framework, diffRL, we conduct an extensive empirical study across three representative DRL-based control systems -- adaptive video streaming, wireless resource allocation, and congestion control -- covering both discrete and continuous action spaces. Through these case studies, we analyze symbolic properties over broad input ranges, examine how property satisfaction evolves during training, study the impact of model size on verifiability, and compare multiple verification backends. Our results show that symbolic properties provide substantially broader coverage than point properties and can uncover non-obvious, operationally meaningful counterexamples, while also revealing practical solver trade-offs and limitations.

openalex.abstract: The rapid evolution of fifth-generation (5G) and emerging sixth-generation (6G) communication technologies has significantly transformed the telecommunications industry by enabling ultra-high-speed connectivity, intelligent network automation, and massive Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. Despite these advancements, modern telecom networks continue to encounter challenges related to network congestion, resource allocation, service reliability, cybersecurity, fault diagnosis, and energy consumption. Conventional Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques have demonstrated considerable success in predictive analytics and network optimization; however, they often fail to distinguish correlation from causation, limiting their effectiveness in dynamic environments where decisions must be explainable and adaptable. This research presents a comprehensive framework that integrates Causal Artificial Intelligence (Causal AI), Large Language Models (LLMs), and advanced AI/ML algorithms to develop next-generation intelligent telecom networks capable of autonomous reasoning, predictive maintenance, intelligent traffic engineering, anomaly detection, and self-healing operations. Causal AI enables root-cause identification and explainable decision-making, while LLMs provide natural language interaction, intelligent knowledge retrieval, and automated operational assistance for telecom engineers. Traditional AI/ML algorithms including Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Networks, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Reinforcement Learning, and Graph Neural Networks contribute to predictive analytics and adaptive optimization.

openalex.display_name: Position: Profiling Game Worlds by Transition Complexity
openalex.abstract: Game world modeling (GWM) and reinforcement learning (RL) are often confounded because research papers rarely quantify how difficult the underlying transition prediction problem is at the declared interface (pixels/tokens/latents with finite history). We propose the Transition Complexity Profile (TCP): a small, reproducible set of metrics that characterizes an environment's (or gameplay dataset's) induced transition kernel by (i) intrinsic one-step branching, (ii) interaction-induced uncertainty and opponent influence when observable, and (iii) temporal/spatial dependency span via standardized probe curves. TCP is reported with an explicit reference distribution, protocol stochasticity, and a versioned measurement budget (sampling/resampling and fixed probe compute), enabling comparable numbers across benchmarks. We outline how common game families and modern "neural game engine" domains populate this landscape and call for TCP to become standard benchmark metadata and a required statistic in GWM and RL papers.

openalex.abstract: Real-time video streaming over RTP/RTCP is challenged by delayed feedback, random wireless losses, and timevarying bandwidth, which often degrade the performance of conventional congestion control methods. To address these issues, this paper proposes PRO-SAC, a deep reinforcement learning-based congestion control framework for continuous bitrate adaptation in real-time streaming. By integrating temporal state reconstruction, reward-guided active probing, and a lower-bounded entropy temperature mechanism, the proposed method enhances delayedfeedback perception, sustained exploration, and training stability. Experimental results on a GStreamer-based end-to-end testbed show that PRO-SAC consistently outperforms AIMD under both staircase-bandwidth and dynamic wireless scenarios. Under the configured dynamic network scenario, PRO-SAC achieves an average bitrate of 1656.05 kbps, an average packet loss rate of $\mathbf{1. 9 6 \%}$, an average RTT of $\mathbf{1 3 3. 2 7 ~ m s}$, and a 90th-percentile RTT of 254.1 ms, compared with 1565.67 kbps, 8.16%, 185.21 ms, and 380.5 ms for AIMD, respectively. These results demonstrate that PRO-SAC provides a better throughput-delay tradeoff and stronger robustness for real-time streaming applications.

openalex.abstract: Aiming at the problems of high latency, high bit error rate and susceptibility to imbalance in multi-flow competition for the bottleneck link on return links of GEO satellites, the traditional rule-based TCP variants fail to distinguish bit errors from network congestion, and the single-agent reinforcement learning cannot realize global collaboration, resulting in unsatisfactory fairness and link utilization. To tackle solve these issues, this paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm named MaGEO-CC. The multi-flow TCPs transmission process at the terminal is modeled as a multi-agent Markov decision process. A globally and locally fused state space is constructed to mitigate non-Markovian problems, and a composite reward function that balances transmission efficiency and fairness is designed. The coordinated multi-flow control is realized based on the centralized training and decentralized execution framework. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm maintains stable transmission under dynamic scenarios with a fairness index between 0.97 and 0.98, which can well adapt to the inherent characteristics of satellite links.

openalex.abstract: Optimization of traffic allocation has emerged as an important problem in telecommunication transport networks due to increasingly dynamic network conditions and exponential growth in data traffic requirements. Traditional transport engineering approaches, including heuristic-based and traditional reinforcement learning methods, struggle to quickly adapt to the often-evolving traffic patterns, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization, network congestion, and poor service quality. This article offers an in-depth study-based framework for optimizing real-time traffic distribution that takes advantage of the predictive capabilities of hybrid neural network architectures. In the proposed approach, convolutional neural networks (CNN) are used for long-term short-term memory (LSTM) networks to extract spatial features from network topology data and identify a temporal pattern in traffic flow. A comparative analysis with modern reinforcement learning methods, particularly the critical flow direction with weight gain learning (CFR-RL), shows that deep learning achieves high traffic prediction accuracy (85-90% versus 92-97%), faster approach during training, and stable operation in a variety of networking conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed Deep Learning (DL)-based approach reduces end-to-end latency by 23-35% compared to Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based methods, improves network resource utilization by up to 28%, and maintains consistent quality of service guarantees for high priority traffic flows. In addition, educational model exhibits excellent scalability features, maintaining a summary delay below 15ms for networks with up 500 nodes. These findings establish in-depth learning as an extensible, practical and highly efficient solution to optimize traffic distribution in a new generation of telecommunication transport networks.

openalex.abstract: Congestion control (CC) is a decades-old open problem: algorithms must continuously balance throughput maximization against queue buildup and packet loss. Classical algorithms - TCP Reno, CUBIC, and BBR rely on hand-crafted heuristics that can fail to generalize. Learned approaches such as Aurora improve adaptability through deep reinforcement learning but sacrifice interpretability and can overfit to simulator dynamics. We present an approach that reframes CC as a language reasoning task. A 1.5-billion-parameter LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) is prompted with the current network observation along with five few shot examples. The model produces an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning before committing to a discrete rate-multiplier. We then fine-tuning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with LoRA, following the One-Shot-RLVR paradigm. The reward signal is adapted from PCC Vivace and jointly penalizes queue growth and packet loss while rewarding link utilization, with policy gradients masked to the action tokens only. We describe the full system design and training methodology.

openalex.abstract: The exponential growth of cloud computing has intensified the conflict between minimizing data center energy consumption and adhering to strict Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Existing heuristic algorithms often suffer from response latency, while standard Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods tend to compromise system safety in their pursuit of energy rewards. To reconcile these objectives, this paper proposes Informer-PCPO, a novel virtual machine scheduling framework that integrates long-term time-series forecasting with probabilistic constrained optimization. First, an Informer-based state encoder is introduced to capture long-range workload dependencies via sparse self-attention, overcoming the limitations of traditional LSTMs to achieve accurate future load perception. Second, to ensure safety, we propose the Probabilistic Constrained Policy Optimization (PCPO) algorithm. By utilizing Lagrangian multipliers, PCPO transforms hard constraints-such as SLA violations and network congestion-into dynamic soft penalties, enabling the agent to aggressively explore energy-saving strategies while proactively averting risks. Extensive simulations using real-world cloud traces demonstrate that Informer-PCPO significantly reduces average energy consumption compared to baselines while maintaining near-zero SLA violations. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis confirms the framework's high controllability, achieving a Pareto-optimal trade-off between energy efficiency and reliability under varying constraint targets.

openalex.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been widely applied to optimize unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)assisted communication networks. However, most existing MARL algorithms rely on an idealized assumption that agents are connected by continuous, synchronized, and flawless communication links. In realistic and complex communication environments, severe interference and network congestion often cause frequent burst packet losses and time-varying delays, leading to sudden breakdowns in multi-agent coordination. To address this challenge, this paper departs from the constraints of traditional discrete-time communication models and proposes a continuoustime asynchronous communication framework based on Resilient Intent Dynamics Extrapolation (RIDE). RIDE unifies packet loss and delay as irregular asynchronous event streams and introduces a time-aware Flow-Jump process to continuously extrapolate teammate latent states during communication interruptions and instantly correct the extrapolated results when delayed packets arrive, thereby mitigating the information vacuum caused by packet loss and the temporal misalignment caused by delay. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RIDE maintains highly effective coordination under high packet loss rates and severe dynamic delays, while its extremely small computational overhead makes it well suited for edge-computing deployment.

openalex.abstract: No single congestion control (CC) algorithm performs well across heterogeneous and time-varying network conditions. While loss-based, delay-based, and hybrid designs excel in specific regimes, they degrade outside them. Conversely, fully learned CC approaches offer adaptability but raise concerns regarding interpretability and deployment safety. Consequently, today’s systems lack a robust mechanism to dynamically select the optimal strategy during an active connection. We address this gap with ALCHEMY, a framework that enables adaptive CC selection in QUIC. ALCHEMY introduces a state-preserving midstream switching mechanism that allows CC algorithms to be safely changed within an ongoing connection without triggering slow-start resets or control instability. Building on this capability, ALCHEMY employs an offline-trained deep reinforcement learning policy to select the most appropriate expert algorithm at runtime using cross-layer transport signals. Rather than replacing existing CC logic, ALCHEMY orchestrates established heuristics, leveraging their complementary strengths. Implemented in a high-fidelity emulated QUIC stack and evaluated across 26 diverse network scenarios, ALCHEMY demonstrates superior adaptability compared to static baselines. It improves the scenario-wise winning rate by approximately 29% relative to the best-performing individual heuristic CC algorithm. Here, winning rate denotes the frequency of achieving the highest composite throughput–delay score among all evaluated schemes. Unlike static algorithms that are bound to a fixed design envelope, ALCHEMY consistently maintains near-optimal throughput-delay trade-offs across heterogeneous and volatile regimes.

openalex.abstract: As the types and scale of applications supported by data center networks continue to expand, network traffic characteristics are becoming increasingly complex, exhibiting high dynamism and heterogeneity in both time and space dimensions. Efficient congestion control technology is crucial to optimizing network performance. Adaptive adjustment mechanisms for congestion control parameters based on distributed switches and centralized controllers often exhibit limitations when handling complex and changing traffic characteristics, resulting in poor network performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CoPT, a Collaborative machine-learningbased mechanism for adaptive congestion control Parameter Tuning in data center networks. This mechanism uses a network performance model in the centralized controller to predict portlevel ECN parameters for global network traffic and sends the predictions as “guidance” to the switch control plane. A guided-reinforcement-learning-based agent is deployed on the distributed switch ports. This agent, combined with local traffic characteristics and global ECN parameters, “guides” the selection of optimal parameters, effectively adapting to various complex traffic characteristics and significantly improving network performance. Experimental results show that, under various traffic scenarios, CoPT significantly outperforms both distributed-based and centralized-based methods in terms of flow completion time (FCT) and reduction of average queue length.

openalex.abstract: Real-time video streaming (RVS) has become the Internet’s dominant application, supporting latency-critical services from telemedicine to remote collaboration. However, stringent latency requirements force RVS systems to rely on UDP-based transport that tolerates packet loss, creating reliability challenges. Packet loss, whether from congestion or transmission errors, creates two irreconcilable failure modes: if corrupted reference frames are displayed, prediction errors propagate through all dependent frames, causing severe visual degradation; if packets are retransmitted aggressively, latency accumulates beyond real-time tolerances. This dilemma cannot be resolved within either layer independently: transport-layer mechanisms like retransmission or FEC exacerbate congestion, while codec-layer solutions like bitrate reduction degrade visual quality.We present RAPIDS, a codec-transport co-design that resolves this impasse through dynamic dependency restructuring. RAPIDS employs a deep reinforcement learning controller to adaptively designate frames as reference or non-reference based on real-time network conditions, effectively decoupling frame importance from encoding structure. This semantic information guides a partially reliable QUIC transport to implement differentiated protection: critical reference frames receive guaranteed delivery via retransmission, while non-reference frames can be proactively discarded under congestion to bound latency. Extensive evaluation on 1000+ real-world network traces demonstrates 28-50% QoS improvement over WebRTC, Salsify, and SODA, with a 4-5× faster error recovery during traffic bursts and network outages.

openalex.abstract: Internet congestion control (CC) aims to efficiently utilize bandwidth while maintaining low latency under diverse network conditions. Recent advances in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) provide a promising approach; however, online DRL usually suffers from data inefficiency and delayed network feedback. In this work, we formulate congestion control as an offline reinforcement learning problem using datasets collected from multiple existing CC algorithms. While such multi-source data encodes rich prior knowledge, their heterogeneous distributions can lead to Q-value overestimation in offline learning. To address this issue, we propose POCC, an offline RL approach with pessimistic Q-value estimation, leveraging an ensemble of critic networks to reduce overestimation. This design enables stable and safe policy learning from heterogeneous congestion control data, realizing robust CC policies across diverse network environments. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that POCC obtains superior performance by reducing the average latency by up to 77% compared to existing approaches under different dynamic bandwidth conditions.

openalex.abstract: Continuous Integration pipelines are supposed to provide immediate feedback regarding faults after each commit. But performing a complete testing phase during every build is often too expensive. TCP addresses this problem by rearranging the test sequence in such a way that tests with the greatest chance of failure detection occur earlier in the process. We present TFPE-DQN, a Deep Q-Network agent whose input is a compact four-dimensional Temporal Failure Pattern Encoding (TFPE) derived solely from historical CI execution logs and no source-code instrumentation is required. TFPE combines a sliding-window recent failure rate, a cumulative long-horizon failure rate, a within-cycle z-score normalized duration, and a binary above-median duration flag. Learning is shaped by a Duration-Aware Reward (DAR) that rewards early fault detection and penalizes proportionally to the normalized execution time of passing tests. Evaluated on the public Kaggle Test-Case Prioritization dataset (604 tests, 106 CI cycles, 64,024 records), TFPE-DQN converges to an APFD of 0.8932 — equalling the theoretical ceiling — within five training episodes, and sustains zero variance across all 27 held-out evaluation cycles. Against a random ordering baseline (APFD ≈ 0.50) and a shortest-first heuristic (APFD = 0.5454), the gains are 78.0% and 63.7% respectively.

openalex.abstract: The rapid deployment of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) necessitates highly reliable and low-latency Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication networks. As traffic density increases, static communication routing leads to severe network congestion, degrading the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) and increasing critical safety latency. To address this challenge, we propose a novel hybrid Digital Twin framework that bridges a physical hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) prototype with a scalable traffic simulation. Our architecture maps real-world perception data from an RC car prototype, equipped with a Raspberry Pi and edge-based perception, into a continuous Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) environment. Furthermore, we formulate the dynamic V2X mode selection problem—switching between Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) networks—as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Using a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning agent, our system dynamically allocates communication modes to optimize the trade-off between the high reliability of V2I and the ultra-low latency of V2V. Experimental results from the synchronized Digital Twin indicate that the proposed PPO-based adaptive controller reduces average communication latency relative to a static V2I baseline while maintaining near-perfect simulated packet delivery performance under varying traffic densities.

Previous research on robotic DLOs manipulation has primarily addressed quasi-static DLO manipulation at low speeds, leaving the potential of dynamic DLO manipulation largely unexplored. source.display_name: UNSWorks (University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia)

openalex.abstract: The proliferation of wireless services and devices is intensifying the demand for wireless spectral resources, resulting in instances of spectrum congestion and interception of wireless communications. The spectrum allocation models currently adopted by wireless network operators are semi-static and coarse-grained, and do not provide sufficient protection anymore against congestion and eavesdropping anymore. In a congested spectrum scenario, it is also difficult to differentiate jamming attacks from a legitimate network congestion condition and detect eavesdropping in situations with a high density of devices. Our hypothesis is that finegrained, dynamic cooperation among network operators based on the principles of the sharing economy can play a critical role in addressing these challenges. The primary aim of this research is to design and investigate a framework to enable dynamic trading of radio resources among wireless network operators based on their users’ quality of service and security requirements. This framework contrasts strongly with traditional systems where operators act in isolation without considering user requirements. We have shown that such a framework can indeed be designed and implemented by adopting novel technologies such as wireless network programmability, physical-layer security, and deep reinforcement learning. We demonstrated how a centralized programmable network architecture can enable cooperation among wireless operators, with deep reinforcement learning facilitating quasi-continuous optimization of radio resources in a dynamic multi-operator environment. Finally, we considered economic incentives among wireless operators and users to entice them in the process of trading these resources. Evaluation results show that the proposed trading framework can significantly improve user satisfaction, compared to the current static and coarse-grained approaches. It also enables cooperative network operators to act as jammers to protect against eavesdropping in a multi-operator environment. More specifically, the framework allows dynamic negotiation and trading of radio resources among independent operators to meet the throughput or secure throughput requirements of their users. Overall, this research contributes new dynamic, adaptive, market-oriented trading mechanisms for network operators of wireless communication systems to optimize spectral efficiency while satisfying the quality of service and security requirements of users.

openalex.abstract: With the widespread adoption of Wi-Fi 7 in campus networks, high-density access and large-scale research data transmission challenge traditional congestion control algorithms. TCP-bottleneck bandwidth and round-trip propagation time (BBR) lacks deep link awareness and service semantic breadth, leading to misinterpreting non-congestive packet loss and inter-flow unfairness in complex wireless scenarios. To address this, this paper proposes semantic-aware and cross-layer collaborative optimized BBR (SAC-BBR), a semantic-aware cross-layer optimization mechanism for high-density heterogeneous campus networks. It leverages an Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) to capture physical link characteristics in real time within the Linux kernel, accurately distinguishing random loss from congestion loss. It then constructs a lightweight semantic identification engine to classify traffic and establish a service satisfaction utility model. Finally, a deep reinforcement learning-based dynamic gain regulator maps cross-layer states and service priorities to the action space, enabling millisecond-level intelligent tuning of pacing_gain and cwnd_gain. Experimental results show that SAC-BBR improves throughput by over 22% compared to BBRv3 and reduces average round-trip time (RTT) by 17% while suppressing RTT jitter by over 60% in high-density scenarios. Furthermore, it enhances the Jain fairness index to 0.93 under multi-protocol competition, ensuring high-performance and equitable transmission.

openalex.abstract: High renewable penetration and large-scale electric vehicle integration impose voltage instability, frequency deviation, and network congestion challenges in distribution systems while accelerating battery degradation. This study proposes a degradation constrained multi agent reinforcement learning framework based on centralized training with decentralized execution for coordinated vehicle to grid optimization. The method integrates DC power flow constraints, stochastic renewable uncertainty, and electrochemical battery aging dynamics within a unified control architecture to ensure network aware and lifecycle aware scheduling. The framework is evaluated on the IEEE 33 bus distribution network with electric vehicle penetration up to 50% and compared against two baselines: a rule based conventional V2G scheduler and a single agent deep reinforcement learning controller without coordinated network constraints or degradation penalization. Grid stability is quantified using a normalized composite index derived from frequency and voltage magnitude deviations. Across repeated simulation trials, the proposed approach improves the mean stability index by approximately 10% relative to the rule-based method and 7% relative to the single agent baseline. Renewable utilization increases by about 18% age points, peak load reduction reaches 40% under high penetration scenarios, and cumulative battery aging decreases by nearly 13% over a 24-hour horizon, demonstrating enhanced coordinated control performance within standardized simulation environments.

openalex.abstract: Fog computing has emerged as a promising paradigm to extend cloud services closer to IoT devices, improving response times & reducing network congestion. However, efficient load balancing in fog computing is essential to maximize performance, reduce costs, ensure energy efficiency, & maintain a high quality of service, ultimately supporting the demands of latency-sensitive & resource-intensive IoT applications. The primary objective of task mapping in computing environments such as cloud, fog, & edge computing is to allocate tasks across available resources in an efficient & effective manner, particularly in fog computing, where resources are distributed & closer to end devices. This paper presents a hybrid approach that integrates Genetic Algorithm (GA) & Deep Q-Learning (DQL) for task mapping in fog computing environments. The objective is to minimize makespan & computational costs while maintaining high resource utilization. Our approach leverages a GA to perform initial task allocation by exploring a broad solution space, thereby enhancing convergence toward optimal scheduling patterns. This solution is refined using DQL, which adapts to dynamic environments by learning from continuous feedback and enabling real-time decision-making. By combining the exploration strengths of GA with the adaptive capabilities of DQL, the proposed method effectively manages task allocation & resource utilization. Experimental results show that our hybrid approach outperforms baseline methods, significantly reducing makespan & operational costs.

openalex.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging networks face major operational challenges, including demand uncertainty, peak-load congestion, and anomalous charging behavior, particularly in multi-station environments. This study proposes an anomaly-aware Q-learning framework for real-time scheduling in multi-station EV charging systems by integrating short-term load forecasting, anomaly detection, and intelligent scheduling within a unified operational pipeline. The framework combines Prophet, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models for short-term demand forecasting, while Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Autoencoders, and Isolation Forests are employed for anomaly detection. Forecasting and anomaly information are incorporated into a Q-learning scheduler to support adaptive charger allocation and congestion management. Evaluation using a four-year, real-world dataset comprising more than 2000 EV charging sessions demonstrates improved scheduling performance, achieving reductions in peak load and waiting time while improving energy delivery consistency. The framework further demonstrates low scheduling latency, supporting suitability for real-time deployment in OCPP-compliant smart charging infrastructures.

openalex.display_name: AI-HierSFL: Three-Tier Split Federated Learning for Energy-Efficient 6G Networks
openalex.abstract: Distributed learning in communication-constrained networks faces a critical bottleneck: balancing model performance against limited bandwidth and fluctuating channel conditions. We introduce AI-HierSFL, a three-tier framework that optimizes communication efficiency through proactive resource orchestration. Unlike static split learning approaches, AI-HierSFL integrates Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) to dynamically allocate bandwidth and computational resources, Time-series Generative Adversarial Networks (TimeGAN) to predict network congestion for adaptive aggregation, and Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS) to optimize split points in real-time. We formulate a joint optimization problem minimizing energy and communication costs subject to local differential privacy constraints, providing rigorous convergence guarantees for non-convex loss functions. Comprehensive evaluations on CIFAR-10/100 and MNIST benchmarks demonstrate that AI-HierSFL reduces communication overhead by 12.8% and total energy consumption by 30.4% compared to FedAvg, establishing it as a robust solution for distributed optimization in resource-constrained environments.

openalex.abstract: Providing seamless global Internet connectivity remains a significant challenge due to geographical barriers, economic constraints, and vulnerabilities to catastrophic events, including natural disasters and warfare. Non-terrestrial Networks (NTN), particularly satellite communication systems, are crucial for overcoming these limitations, but traditional geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) satellites experience inherent latency issues due to their high-altitude positioning. Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites have emerged as superior alternatives, significantly reducing communication delays and enhancing network performance. Despite their advantages, LEO satellite networks face significant challenges arising from rapidly changing network topologies driven by high orbital speeds, resulting in frequent shifts in inter-satellite link (ISL) availability. Conventional routing algorithms struggle to adapt effectively to these dynamic conditions, resulting in suboptimal routing decisions and increased latency due to congestion-related issues. To address these complexities, this paper proposes an adaptive reinforcement learning-based NTN routing (ARL-NTNR) algorithm designed explicitly for dynamic LEO environments. The proposed ARL-NTNR algorithm autonomously learns and adapts optimal routing policies in real-time by continually interacting with the evolving satellite network. It effectively balances shortest-path routing with real-time queue backlog congestion management, significantly reducing packet delay and minimizing packet loss.

primary_location.raw_source_name: Computer Science and Engineering Master's Theses

openalex.abstract: Despite decades of progress in network protocols and control algorithms, many network-control mechanisms continue to rely on fixed heuristics, manually written rules, or static controller logic. This thesis explores the use of large language models as reasoning-based decision-making components within networked systems. The thesis presents two case studies. The first, RLVR-CC, investigates whether a large language model can be trained to make congestion-control decisions using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. In this system, the model observes network state, reasons about current conditions, and selects a rate-control action. The second, Agent-Defined Networking, studies whether a large language model can participate in software-defined networking control-plane decisions, including natural-language policy compilation, runtime firewall enforcement, and congestion-aware routing. Together, these systems examine the potential and limitations of incorporating large language models into network infrastructure. The results suggest that language models can support network decision-making when their outputs are bounded by reward functions, validation checks, and safety guardrails.

openalex.abstract: This paper proposes an Adaptive Request Routing Framework (ARRF) to reduce latency in edge-cloud continuum environments. Traditional cloud routing often suffers from delays due to network congestion and static policies. ARRF dynamically selects the best computing node (edge, fog, or cloud) for each request using real-time metrics such as latency, CPU usage, memory, queue length, and bandwidth. Experimental results show that ARRF reduces latency by 58.6%, achieves 98.1% QoS satisfaction, and improves resource utilization compared to existing methods like Round Robin and reinforcement learning-based routing. This framework provides a scalable solution for latency-sensitive applications including autonomous vehicles, smart cities, and healthcare IoT.

openalex.abstract: Modern IP networks face significant challenges in maintaining performance under dynamic and diverse traffic conditions. Traditional congestion control algorithms, such as TCP Reno, Cubic, and even recent reinforcement learning (RL) methods like PPO and DQN, often respond uniformly to packet loss, failing to distinguish between congestion-induced losses and those arising from wireless interference or hardware failures. This paper introduces AHMA (Adaptive Hierarchical Meta-Agent) — a novel, two-stage intelligent congestion control framework that integrates a Bayesian Transformer-based classifier with a Meta-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (Meta-ES-RL) controller. AHMA first classifies the cause of packet loss in real-time and then dynamically selects an optimized control strategy based on classification confidence. Using a synthetically generated NS-3 dataset of 1000 labeled flow samples, we evaluate AHMA’s performance against PPO, DQN, TCP Cubic, and TCP Reno across key metrics. Experimental results show that AHMA achieves a decision accuracy of 92%, reduces packet loss to 8.56% with improved throughput, and decreased latency, outperforming all baseline methods. This approach represents a significant advancement in adaptive, cause-aware congestion management, with strong potential for deployment in next-generation high-performance IP and 5G networks.

openalex.abstract: Traffic congestion prediction is a significant technique adapted for improving the Vehicle Ad-hoc Network performance through effective avoidance of network delay and network congestion. Early traffic management strategies have significant limitations in adapting to the dynamic changes in the network traffic, resulting in increased computational complexity and inefficient management of the network resources. Hence, the research develops an effective Reinforcement Learning-based Convolutional Neural Network-Light Gradient Boosting Machine (RCGBM) model to anticipate the vehicular congestion. The integration of the Reinforcement Learning mechanism increases the flexibility of the network to adaptive congestion control via the usage of an appropriate reward function. Further, the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN)-based imputation enables efficient acquisition of the complex spatial and temporal characteristics of the traffic data. Moreover, aggregation of the network data from diverse Road Side Units (RSUs) reduces the workload and aids in efficient computational resource utilization. In addition, the integration of the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) to analyse the network traffic data reduces the computational complexity and aids in the effective management of the networking resources. Numerical assessment exemplifies the traffic congestion prediction superiority of the research by attaining 97.93% accuracy, 98.12% specificity, and 97.74% sensitivity for 90% training.

openalex.abstract: Modern Software-Defined Wide Area Networks (SD- WANs) require agile traffic steering to satisfy diverse Quality of Service (QoS) demands across volatile multi-path environments. Conventional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approaches often suffer from state aliasing and fail to mitigate tail latency spikes for mission-critical traffic. In this paper, we propose a temporal-aware DRL framework for dynamic load balancing, utilizing a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architecture integrated with autoregressive action feedback. Our approach employs a hi- erarchical, P99-aware reward function that enforces strict Service Level Agreement (SLA) barriers for Expedited Forwarding (EF) traffic. Evaluated in an ns-3 environment, our agent demonstrates superior stability and convergence compared to vanilla PPO and UCMP baselines. Experimental results show that the recurrent architecture significantly reduces EF tail latency and packet loss, ensuring robust performance for real-time applications even during sustained periods of network congestion.

openalex.display_name: Integrasi dan Evaluasi Sistem Deteksi DDoS Berbasis Deep Reinforcement Learning Pada Lingkungan Internet of Things Menggunakan Honeypot

source.display_name: UMM Institutional Repository (University of Maine at Machias)

openalex.abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) increases the risk of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, especially because many IoT devices have limited resources and simple security mechanisms. This study integrates a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) DDoS detection system in a gateway IoT test environment using RIoTPot honeypot as a traffic sensor. The system is built using several virtual machines that function as the honeypot, DRL node, gateway, traffic generator, and monitoring node. A Dueling DQN model based on Saif et al. (2024) is integrated into a detection pipeline that includes PCAP conversion, flow-based feature extraction, model inference, result logging to PostgreSQL, and visualization through Grafana. The evaluation is conducted on seven DDoS scenarios, including TCP SYN flood on several service ports, UDP flood, ICMP flood, and multi-vector DDoS. The results show that recall is close to 1.0 across all scenarios, with accuracy ranging from 0.979 to 0.996 and F1-score ranging from 0.989 to 0.998. Specificity ranges from 0.340 to 0.738, indicating that the model still needs improvement in distinguishing normal traffic. In addition to detection, the system also applies simple rate-limiting mitigation on the gateway. The test results show that the system can detect attacks effectively while maintaining relatively low resource usage. Therefore, a DRL DDoS detection system can be integrated with a honeypot and gateway in an IoT environment.
