openalex.abstract: The aggregation of concurrent Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) data traffic from distributed sites to the cloud frequently induces uplink congestion at the capacityconstrained cloud infrastructure ingress. Conventional reactive congestion control mechanisms are constrained by inherent feedback delays, while static bandwidth allocation strategies fail to adapt to stochastic traffic fluctuations, resulting in resource underutilization during off-peak periods and packet loss during bursts. To address these limitations, we propose a recurrent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for proactive bandwidth orchestration. By integrating gated recurrent units (GRUs) into the policy architecture, the framework extracts latent temporal features from historical network observations, thereby capturing the underlying dynamics of bursty traffic. Driven by these temporal features, the DRL agent proactively regulates gateway transmission rates, mitigating ingress congestion and protecting mission-critical flows against packet loss. Performance evaluations under realistic industrial traffic profiles demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces sample complexity by over 50% compared to memoryless DRL and heuristic baselines, while constraining the ingress packet loss rate to$\mathbf{1. 2 0 \%}$under heavy saturation.

openalex.abstract: Standard Reinforcement Learning techniques break down to address some very common conditions in edge computing like new workload types, network fluctuations and other unseen scenarios. These techniques rely on correlating to traditional patterns such as if there is more latency then increase the resources like CPU etc. to reduce the delay. To address this core problem in this paper, Causal Reinforcement Learning(CRL) is introduced for adaptive resource management in edge cloud computing environments that will help identify cause-effect relationships. CRL learns that the high latency is due to network congestion and not CPU load. This helps in analyzing the problem and rerouting the path instead of allocating more CPUs in edge computing infrastructure. CRL handles distribution shifts in real systems where the workload is non stationary and patterns changes over time. This is handled using causal structure that generalizes to unseen situations. The proposed approach in this paper addresses more reliable decision making through intervention aware learning which makes Distributed Systems more robust, reliable and explainable. The framework employs Domain Informed Causal Graph to capture relationships in workload, resource utilization, network conditions and task latency. Causal feature extraction will enable it to capture the priority tasks in the scheduler and eliminate spurious correlations that will improve adaptive decision making under dynamic operating conditions. Experimental evaluation using Google Cluster workload Trace and Alibaba Cluster Trace Dataset along with synthetic workload perturbations to emulate distribution shifts. This approach followed heterogeneous Edge-Cloud environments and a CRL framework to reduce the task latency from 318ms to 162ms when compared to FCFS scheduler and from 208ms to 162 ms when compared to DQN baseline. The resource utilization also increased from 79% to 89% and the speed affected by 28.6% under dynamic workload variations. These results indicated integrating causal reasoning with reinforcement learning highly likely improved the scheduling robustness, resource utilization and adaptive decision making in Distributed Cloud Edge systems.

openalex.abstract: Virtual machine (VM) placement in cloud data centers involves deciding how incoming VM requests should be mapped onto available physical machines while respecting resource capacities, service-level agreements (SLAs), and energy efficiency requirements. This problem becomes challenging in large-scale cloud environments due to continuously changing workloads, heterogeneous resource demands, and network traffic interactions between VMs. Improper placement decisions lead to resource imbalance, increased power consumption, SLA violations, and network congestion. To address these challenges, this paper presents a structured multi-objective VM placement framework that combines evolutionary optimization with reinforcement learning to support both solution quality and adaptive decision-making. The proposed framework operates in two coordinated stages. In the first stage, an evolutionary optimization module generates candidate VM-to-host placement solutions by encoding VM requests and physical machine capacities as individuals and evaluating them using explicit objective functions, including VM acceptance ratio, CPU and memory utilization balance, energy consumption of active servers, and estimated network communication cost. This stage performs global exploration of the placement search space and identifies Pareto-efficient solutions under resource and SLA constraints. In the second stage, a reinforcement learning agent observes the real-time state of the data center, including host utilization levels, workload arrival patterns, and network load indicators, and selects placement or migration actions to refine the evolutionary solutions. A reward function is designed to explicitly penalize energy waste, resource overload, SLA violations, and network congestion, while encouraging balanced utilization and efficient VM admission. By integrating global evolutionary search with online learning-based adaptation, the proposed framework enables stable and scalable VM placement under dynamic cloud workloads. Simulation-based evaluation demonstrates consistent improvements in VM acceptance, energy efficiency, resource utilization balance, and SLA compliance compared to conventional heuristic, evolutionary-only, and learning-only placement strategies.

openalex.abstract: This article reviews the evolution of cable television distribution, from coaxial networks to virtualized architectures based on the internet protocol and the cloud, and examines how artificial intelligence has transformed the bitrate adaptation (ABR) algorithms that underpin HTTP Adaptive Streaming (HAS) throughout that transition. Peer-reviewed academic literature and industry documentation were reviewed, and the managed and best-effort distribution models on which these algorithms operate were characterized, alongside the ongoing transport-layer shift from TCP to QUIC. The analysis identifies four fronts where artificial intelligence intervenes at different points of the distribution chain, bitrate decision-making through deep reinforcement learning, content-aware encoding, client-side super-resolution, and energy-aware adaptation, each backed by quantitative gains of up to 43% in quality of experience over a strong reinforcement-learning baseline and up to 57% in energy consumption relative to state-of-the-art algorithms. The article concludes that the sophistication of these models is systematically in tension with the real-time decision requirement of live streaming, which positions coordination across fronts, rather than the isolated improvement of each one, as the central challenge facing the industry.

openalex.abstract: Evaluating congestion control is inherently challenging because performance depends on the interaction between the congestion-control algorithm, transport stack, application behaviour, measurement process, and network dynamics. This challenge is growing as state-of-the-art protocols incorporate pacing, selective loss recovery, model-based control, and, more recently, reinforcement learning. Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are a particularly demanding setting: rapidly changing paths, handovers, non-congestive loss, RTT variation, and transient hotspots all affect transport behaviour. This paper reports the lessons learned from an extensive evaluation campaign across both simulation and emulation for LEO satellite congestion control. We compare multiple classes of congestion-control algorithms, including Cubic, BBR variants, LEO-specific protocols, and reinforcement-learning-based control, using comparable implementations across OMNeT++/INET simulation and Mininet-based emulation with the Linux transport stack. This gives us a rare opportunity to examine not only protocol performance, but also the methodological strengths and limitations of each experimental environment. Our findings show that simulation is indispensable for constellation-scale exploration, controlled parameter sweeps, and future deployment studies, but can miss behaviours caused by production transport-stack mechanisms such as pacing, SACK, RACK, kernel timing, and rate sampling. Emulation exposes these implementation-dependent effects and provides a necessary validation step, but is harder to scale and less exactly repeatable. We distil these experiences into practical lessons for combining simulation and emulation to obtain results that are scalable, reproducible, and deployment-relevant.

openalex.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The development of modern power systems imposes stringent requirements on communication networks, including highly dynamic loads, low latency, and high reliability. Although recent Software-Defined Networking routing, link-utilization-aware scheduling, and reinforcement learning-based methods improve path optimization, challenges remain in bottleneck-link perception, congestion feedback, and stable decision-making under dynamic traffic conditions. OBJECTIVES: To counteract problems like delayed response times and inadequate congestion identification in conventional path selection algorithms owing to dynamic link modifications, this research paper presents a path selection model that combines bottleneck link usage and reinforcement learning. METHODS: Under the Software-Defined Networking control architecture, the proposed model incorporates link utilization, Graph Convolutional Network structures, and Gated Recurrent Units, while introducing a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to optimize routing strategies. RESULTS: Experimental results demonstrate that under a 60 Mbit/s load, the proposed method achieves a throughput of 57 Mbit/s, maintains the minimum transmission delay within 0.043 s, and yields a link utilization rate of 89%. In experiments carried out to evaluate dynamic decision-making, the approach for choosing paths adopted by the model averages convergence at the 15th round, resulting in an error rate of 4.2%, minimal load balancing at 0.23, and median latency time in real-time decisions of only 31 ms, which is better than other models. CONCLUSION: These results demonstrate that the model achieves superior state awareness and adaptive routing performance in multi-source heterogeneous networks. The model also exhibits good performance in terms of congestion control and path optimization and hence can be used effectively for intelligent routing in next-generation power communication networks.

openalex.abstract: Introduction: With the rapid development of smart cities, the backbone optical communication networks that underpin them are facing numerous climate-related disaster challenges. Conventional routing protocols such as OSPF, BGP, and SDN have primarily relied on reactive failure recovery mechanisms to manage these networks. In contrast, the integration of a digital twin system with an inter-domain routing intelligence framework allows for proactive management of these communication backbones. Materials and Methods: The inter-domain routing intelligence framework consists of four cohesive components; (1) a digital twin of the smart city optical backbone integrated with live feed video cameras, (2) an LSTM Deep Learning climate-disaster predictor trained on historical disaster data, (3) an adaptive prioritization of video feeds using DQN, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and GNN based algorithms according to the city’s vulnerability, and (4) a decentralized contextual reinforcement learning–based routing protocol for adaptive fault recovery routing decisions. The framework is evaluated against standard TCP performance metrics and existing routing protocols. Results: Reinforcement learning (RL) with the PPO algorithm yielded the fastest convergence time, while the RL-GNN-based combined framework provided the best cumulative returns, yielding not only higher throughput in typical conditions but also lower latency, higher reliability during failures, and recovery of critical video feeds in disaster conditions. Discussion: Results demonstrate that the integration of digital twin technology with reinforcement learning-based routing protocols can improve the resilience, reliability, and adaptability of optical communication network backbones compared with conventional routing protocols. Additionally, simulations indicate that the digital twin and inter-domain routing intelligence framework can maintain communication between smart city safety services during crises. Conclusion: The integration of a digital twin system with an inter-domain routing intelligence framework for smart city optical communication network backbones allows for proactive management of these networks in the face of potential disasters, ultimately enhancing their survivability, reliability, and efficiency.

openalex.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems has intensified the demand for low-latency, computation-aware, and energy-efficient service orchestration across heterogeneous edge and cloud infrastructures. Conventional centralized cloud architectures struggle to satisfy the stringent delay requirements of real-time applications such as autonomous transportation, industrial automation, smart healthcare, intelligent surveillance, and immersive cyber-physical systems. Edge computing reduces response delay by relocating computational intelligence closer to end devices, yet isolated edge infrastructures often suffer from constrained computational resources, unstable workload distribution, and orchestration inefficiencies under dynamic traffic conditions. This paper proposes an intelligent edge–cloud orchestration framework that integrates latency-aware task offloading, adaptive scheduling, and reinforcement learning-driven resource optimization for IoT environments. The proposed architecture dynamically distributes tasks among IoT devices, edge nodes, and cloud datacenters based on network state, task urgency, energy consumption, queue congestion, and computational complexity. The study develops a hybrid orchestration model that combines Deep Q-Network (DQN)-based offloading decisions with priority-aware scheduling and dynamic resource allocation. A multi-objective optimization function minimizes end-to-end latency while simultaneously reducing energy utilization and task failure probability. Simulation-based experiments compare the proposed framework against cloud-only, edge-only, and heuristic offloading baselines under heterogeneous IoT workloads. Results demonstrate significant reductions in average task latency, network congestion, and execution overhead. The proposed orchestration strategy improves latency performance by 31.8%, reduces energy consumption by 24.6%, and increases task completion efficiency under high-load conditions. The findings indicate that intelligent edge–cloud orchestration can substantially improve Quality of Service (QoS) and scalability in next-generation IoT systems. The proposed framework contributes a publication-oriented orchestration methodology suitable for AI-driven networking, smart infrastructure management, and latency-sensitive distributed computing environments. Keywords: Edge computing, cloud orchestration, IoT, task offloading, latency optimization, intelligent scheduling, deep reinforcement learning, mobile edge computing, AI-driven networking, resource allocation.

openalex.display_name: Hybrid SAC for Corrective Congestion Management in AC/DC Transmission Networks
openalex.abstract: Corrective congestion management in a transmission network with embedded HVDC requires coordinating continuous set-points and discrete topological actions under the full nonlinear AC power flow constraints, a mixed-integer nonlinear problem for which no polynomial-time solution is known. This paper formulates the task as a Markov decision process and solves it with a hybrid Soft Actor-Critic agent that handles both action types under one maximum-entropy objective: a squashed-Gaussian head for redispatch and the VSC-HVDC set-point, and two categorical heads trained through the Gumbel-Softmax Straight-Through estimator for generator and line disconnection. Each action subspace carries its own entropy temperature rather than a shared coefficient, and the behaviour of the three is measured. The state is 906-dimensional and covers branch loadings and reactive flows, bus voltages and angles, and the HVDC set-point. On the IEEE 118-bus system extended with a VSC-HVDClink,theagentclears98.6%ofa500-scenariointact-gridbatch and 97.4% of a 500-scenario batch that includes up to three simultaneous branch outages, in a mean of 1.5 and 1.7 corrective steps respectively, with an independent AC verification power flow confirming the resulting states. Inference requires a single forward pass, which makes the policy usable inside an operational decision cycle.

openalex.abstract: Abstract–We propose a Progressive Binding Commitment Framework (PBCF) that redefines data access and revocation management in decentralized cloud environments by decomposing the commitment lifecycle into three cryptographic states: preliminary, intermediate, and verified. Traditional blockchain-based data sharing systems treat every access grant or revocation as a monolithic transaction requiring immediate finality, which introduces significant latency and scalability bottlenecks. The proposed framework addresses this limitation through a staged Merkle-Patricia Trie hashing mechanism embedded within the smart contract layer, where each state corresponds to a progressively stronger binding between the data access grant and the immutable ledger. An adaptive consensus routing module, driven by a deep Q-network reinforcement learning agent, dynamically selects which commitments to finalize based on real-time network conditions such as block production interval, pending transaction queue length, and validator response time. This agent outputs a policy that prioritizes preliminary commitments for routine data exchanges while deferring intermediate-to-verified transitions for sensitive operations, thereby optimizing throughput and reducing delay. Furthermore, the framework integrates asynchronous zero-knowledge proof generation for permission withdrawal queries, enabling revocation notifications to propagate within milliseconds via a dedicated proof-of-stake sidechain without blocking the main chain’s transaction processing. A policy preprocessor computes a sensitivity score for each data object using a gradient-boosted decision tree trained on historical access patterns, which determines the initial commitment state and dynamically adjusts thresholds based on network congestion. The concrete implementation on Hyperledger Fabric v2.5 demonstrates that the system maintains an average data sharing latency under 200 milliseconds for routine operations while cryptographically enforcing sensitive revocations within five seconds, even under 90% network load. The primary contribution lies in the novel integration of progressive cryptographic commitments with adaptive consensus optimization, which fundamentally improves the scalability and responsiveness of decentralized data sharing frameworks.

openalex.abstract: As Network-on-Chip (NoC)-based multiprocessor arrays continue to scale, permanent faults in processing elements (PEs) increasingly jeopardize system reliability and performance. Topology reconfiguration has become a critical mechanism to tolerate such faults by restoring logical interconnects. However, existing heuristic-based methods often struggle to balance communication efficiency, load distribution, and reconfiguration overhead, especially under high fault densities. To address these limitations, this article proposes KM-RL, a two-stage fault-tolerant reconfiguration framework that integrates bipartite matching and reinforcement learning to optimize PE allocation and migration. In the first stage, the allocation of redundant PEs to faulty ones is formulated as a weighted bipartite matching problem and solved optimally using the Kuhn-Munkres algorithm, followed by a layout refinement strategy to improve load balance. The second stage employs Q-learning to guide migration planning, reducing path lengths and alleviating network congestion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that KM-RL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across a wide range of array sizes and fault densities. Static evaluations indicate that KM-RL yields topologies with reduced congestion and shorter path lengths, while dynamic simulations reveal superior communication performance, combined with a 99.8% reduction in reconfiguration time. This framework provides both theoretical and practical support for fault-tolerant communication in NoC-based multiprocessor arrays.

openalex.abstract: Modern power IoT systems feature massive terminal deployment and increasingly diverse service scenarios. Such conditions frequently cause network congestion, packet disorder and unstable transmission, severely undermining overall network performance. Traditional optimization methods cannot adapt to dynamic heterogeneous network environments and lack native compatibility with the widely adopted WAPI security protocol. Addressing these core defects in power IoT transmission, this study builds an integrated communication optimization framework with embedded WAPI security modules. It further proposes SymDistill-CC, a new algorithm serving as the core congestion control component of the framework. It leverages the teacher-student distillation architecture to transform deep reinforcement learning policies into readable symbolic decision trees, offering transparent decision logic, comparable transmission performance and significantly reduced computation overhead. We then put forward the ECN-FPS packet scheduling mechanism. It detects shared bottlenecks via explicit congestion signaling and use forward prediction to mitigate misordered packets, substantially easing buffer pressure on receiving terminals. Finally, we construct a security-aware dynamic retransmission mechanism for power IoT that perceives network states in real-time under the WAPI authentication framework and adaptively selects unicast or multicast retransmission modes to enhance transmission efficiency and resource utilization. Experimental results demonstrate that in simulated WAPI network environments, the proposed methods achieve a 15%–20% throughput improvement, a 42.5% reduction in out-of-order packets and a link utilization up to 88%–90%, with significant advantages also shown in retransmission efficiency and other key metrics, providing an effective solution for constructing secure, efficient, and reliable power IoT communication systems.

openalex.abstract: The rapid evolution of electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing has intensified the need for highly adaptive, efficient, and intelligent material handling systems capable of operating in dynamic production environments. This review examines recent advances in the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for real-time material flow optimization in EV manufacturing ecosystems. It explores how AI-driven perception, decision-making, and predictive analytics enhance the operational capabilities of AMRs, enabling them to respond autonomously to fluctuating production demands, layout constraints, and supply chain uncertainties. The study synthesizes developments in machine learning algorithms, reinforcement learning, computer vision, and digital twin technologies that collectively enable real-time route optimization, task allocation, congestion avoidance, and energy-efficient navigation within smart factories. Particular attention is given to the role of edge computing and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) architectures in facilitating low-latency communication and decentralized intelligence, which are critical for real-time responsiveness. The review also evaluates system level integration challenges, including interoperability with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), scalability, cybersecurity risks, and safety compliance in human-robot collaborative environments. Furthermore, it highlights emerging trends such as swarm intelligence, multi-agent coordination, and adaptive scheduling frameworks that are redefining material flow strategies in EV production lines. By consolidating current research and industrial practices, this paper identifies key performance improvements in throughput, operational efficiency, and cost reduction attributed to AI-AMR integration. It also outlines future research directions, including the development of explainable AI models, resilient control architectures, and sustainable energy aware robotic systems. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive foundation for understanding how AI-enabled AMRs are transforming material flow optimization and shaping the next generation of intelligent EV manufacturing systems.

source.display_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

openalex.abstract: This paper investigates the application of contextual bandit algorithms to optimize network routing decisions. Traditional network routing protocols often rely on static configurations or simple heuristics, failing to adapt effectively to the dynamic and unpredictable nature of network environments. We propose a framework utilizing contextual bandits to learn optimal routing paths in real-time, considering the current context of the network. This context includes factors such as network congestion, latency, and packet loss. The algorithm iteratively learns through interaction, selecting routes that maximize a defined reward function. The core claim is that network routing decisions can be optimized using this adaptive approach. The key mechanism involves implementing a contextual bandit algorithm that dynamically adjusts routing paths based on contextual information. The results demonstrate the potential for significant improvements in network performance, particularly in scenarios with fluctuating network conditions. The use of contextual bandits offers a novel solution to the challenges of static routing and presents a promising avenue for intelligent and adaptive network management.

openalex.abstract: Sealing aerostructures is a critical assembly process in which sealant is deposited between joining parts to prevent material leakage. Currently, robotic sealing systems use open-loop control methods, in the form of rigid robot programs. However, since pneumatic pressure and robot velocity are manually selected, deposition uniformity is highly reliant on an operator's domain knowledge. To overcome this reliance, adaptive control approaches are being developed, but a crucial aspect is missing, the integration of key performance indicators (KPIs) into controller behavior. Although integrating KPIs into an objective function is an accepted optimization approach, there is a lack of multi-objective control approaches applied to the sealant process. This is crucial for developing automated sealing systems capable of achieving desired manufacturing outcomes such as bead width uniformity and cycle time minimization. Reinforcement learning (RL) can align reward functions with manufacturing KPIs. However training is limited by data acquisition costs, which results in significant material waste. This is further compounded by sealant curing in which viscosity changes within hours. Therefore, lengthy data collection would render the trained policy obsolete before deployment. To address these limitations, a Q-learning based multi-variable control framework is developed. This is driven by a synthetic data generation (SDG) pipeline which consumes 13.5ml of material by leveraging the sealant's fundamental characteristics. This data is used to train the Q-learning controller capable of dynamically adjusting pneumatic pressure and tool center point (TCP) velocity to achieve a target bead width. The resulting controller is validated first in simulation, achieving 99.8% success rate when tasked to converge a bead width to within a tolerance of ±0.5mm. The policy is deployed onto a KUKA KR4 R600 robotic sealing cell, achieving 91.1% success rate. These results demonstrate development of a reliable, multi-variable controllers from minimal data that can optimize desired manufacturing KPIs.

openalex.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed system management called Dynamic Topo-Semantic Network Learning (DTSNL). DTSNL leverages reinforcement learning to enable systems to automatically discover and adapt to changes in underlying hardware and software topology. The core idea is to deploy agents, each responsible for a specific network node or resource, which learn both task execution and topological awareness. These agents utilize sensor data, logs, and monitoring information to observe and understand the network topology. The learning objective is to minimize communication latency, maximize resource utilization, and dynamically adjust routing and communication protocols to accommodate topological changes such as node failures, network congestion, or new node additions. A key component is a "topology-aware" reward function that incentivizes agents to learn sensitivity and adaptability to these changes. DTSNL represents a significant advancement over existing network learning methods that typically assume static topologies, offering a robust and self-optimizing solution for complex and dynamic network environments.

routing in 6G networks is a feature that dynamically selects data paths within a live network, adapting to network conditions like congestion, link quality, user mobility and service demands.Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an emerging approach for dynamic routing of 6G networks.Due to the complexity, single-agent RL model is struggled to optimize routing decisions and maximizing a reward function that represents target network objectives.As the scale of the network grew, it became more tedious to train an individual agent.Therefore, a standard Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) model was adapted for dynamic optimal routing in 6G networks.As more agents are added, the states and actions become large in the standard MARL which takes a long time and a more computation to learn.Therefore, this paper proposes a novel MARL using Decentralized Relational Advantage Actor-Critic (MARL-DR-A2C) for improving dynamic routing of 6G networks.The first step is to forecast network congestion parameters like delay, load and queue length based on past data using the Speed-optimized Long Short-Term Memory (SP-LSTM) network.Then, a Multi-Agent Partially Observed Markov Decision Process (MAPOMDP) is used to model the dynamic routing problem.Finally, MARL-DR-A2C performs dynamic routing by utilizing current network performance parameters and forecasted congestion parameters by SP-LSTM.The primary objective of MARL-DR-A2C is to train a decentralized routing policy using deep policy gradients.MARL-DR-A2C allows the distributed determination of a shared routing strategy, which solves the dynamic routing problem.In addition, MARL-DR-A2C uses Base Station (BS) associations into its routing decisions so that agents can benefit from information about similar destinations.Therefore, to optimize network efficiency, this MARL-DR-A2C is constantly learning and adjusting the optimum routing policies.Finally, when compared to other recent models on 6G networks, the MARL-DR-A2C outperforms them in simulations.

openalex.abstract: Congestion control is a fundamental challenge in modern computer networks, particularly in the transport layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack. While traditional algorithms such as TCP Reno and CUBIC have provided foundational approaches, their adaptability to dynamic and complex network environments remains limited. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising solution due to its adaptive, data-driven nature and ability to optimize performance through interaction with the environment. This study presents a comprehensive survey of RL-based congestion control algorithms, categorizing and comparing existing research across four key dimensions: 1. the RL algorithms used (e.g., Q-learning, Deep RL, POMDP); 2. the parameters defined as state, action, and reward; 3. the simulation platforms employed (e.g., NS-3, Pantheon, Mininet); and 4. performance outcomes. The analysis highlights dominant trends in algorithm selection, parameter usage, and implementation environments. Our findings confirm that RL-based approaches often outperform traditional methods in terms of throughput, delay, fairness, and adaptability. Finally, we outline the current research gaps and propose directions for future work in this evolving field.

openalex.abstract: As the Multimedia Internet of Things (M-IoT) evolves, the orchestration of numerous resources that offer support for high-bandwidth, low-latency applications arises as a key challenge. Architecturally, the edge-cloud framework alleviates structural concerns, but the linked nature of compute and data transfer poses problems of resource management. Approaches that tackle task offloading and adaptive transmission that think independently of each other tend to have problems such as user-server cross-region overloads or network congestion. This paper presents JATO, a framework to jointly tackle the problems of adaptive task offloading and transmission optimization using Deep Reinforcement Learning. JATO offers a mono-faceted solution, learning a policy to simultaneously determine the best offloading target and the transmission quality. The framework was implemented for evaluation with a combination of different edge devices in a testbed alongside a simulation environment. JATO recorded a result of 0.9321 as the holistic score of the overall framework endpoint, a score significantly better than that of all the other frameworks that were used as functional baselines. JATO was able to resource optimally with a network lag of 131.65 milliseconds and a network freeze of 0.09% with the resources utilized. This is evidence that offloading and rate control in combination provides better resource elasticity for M-IoT systems.

openalex.abstract: Mobile and 5G networks offer high data rates, yet they remain vulnerable to congestion during emergency events, potentially degrading service for users and first responders. Accurate throughput prediction is essential for optimizing resource allocation in such scenarios. Results show that both models achieve high prediction accuracy, with CNN-Image outperforming CNN-BiLSTM in mean absolute error and training efficiency. The predicted throughput is then integrated into a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning strategy to guide UAV placement. In simulated emergency scenarios, the PPO-based approach significantly improves average user hroughput and service coverage compared to random placement and no UAV support. This work demonstrates the effectiveness ofcombining deep learning and DRL for enhancing network resilience in disaster-stricken areas.

openalex.abstract: Increases in photovoltaic generation, charging of electric vehicles and heat-pump demand challenge operating limits in low-voltage distribution grids. This requires curative curtailment methods that can operate under sparse observability, noisy measurements, and imperfect grid models. Unlike prior end-to-end reinforcement-learning approaches for partially observable curtailment, this work decouples congestion detection and control by combining a random-forest violation pre-classifier with an actor-critic controller, and evaluates its robustness to measurement noise and grid-parameter mismatch. The framework is tested on a real low-voltage grid using synthetic future operating scenarios with low observability and controllability. With accurate grid parameters, the controller reduces total violation magnitude by 98.9%, and this performance remains nearly unchanged under the tested measurement-noise settings. Grid-model mismatch proves to be more challenging, but the controller still mitigates most violations under the tested mismatch assumptions.

openalex.abstract: Active Queue Management (AQM) algorithms rely on static parameters, which limits their ability to adapt to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of modern network traffic. This paper presents the first Systematic Literature Review (SLR) conducted in strict adherence to PRISMA guidelines, mapping the various ML techniques integrated into AQM, the performance metrics improved and the network environment tested. Our review shows that multiple ML methods have been implemented with reinforcement learning being the most dominant approach, delivering satisfying results across various network environments. Supervised learning proves effective in flow classification scenarios, while recent approaches such as federated learning, multi-agent RL and LLM distillation continue the push the boundaries of the field. We identify four open challenges: networking dataset unavailability, single-based reward function in RL techniques, ML vulnerabilities, and cross environment adaptation. This review gives an organized classification of ML-AQM approaches and a well-defined roadmap for future research.

openalex.abstract: Efficient traffic engineering (TE) is paramount for robust congestion control and sustaining high-performance communication in large-scale low earth orbit (LEO) constellations. However, conventional TE paradigms face an inherent trade-off where effective load balancing requires excessive computation times, hindering rapid LEO network adaptability. In this paper, we propose Elephant flow-aware Learning-Accelerated Traffic Engineering (ELATE), a highly scalable TE framework tailored for LEO networks. Exploiting the heavy-tailed distribution of satellite traffic, it decomposes demands into elephant and mice flows, offloading the latter to static shortest paths and focusing the learning framework on the former to reduce problem dimensionality. For the critical yet congestion-inducing elephant flows, we model the LEO network topology as a time-dependent bipartite graph, using graph neural network (GNN) embeddings to capture structural bottlenecks and flow conservation. Leveraging these flow embeddings and modeling each elephant flow as an independent agent within a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework, ELATE replaces the heavy optimization burden with fast execution. This learning-accelerated paradigm enables adaptive, real-time routing decisions, striking a superior balance between load balancing and rapid decision-making. Simulation results show that ELATE outperforms representative baselines by achieving 8-29% lower maximum link utilization (MLU) and yielding substantial $\mathbf{1 1 - 3 2 8 8} \times$ computational speedups.

openalex.abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and demand electrification is increasing the operational complexity of power grids. Reinforcement learning (RL) agents have shown promising performance in real-time congestion management with topology optimization, but quantifying their reliability under unseen operating conditions remains difficult. This paper proposes a framework to quantify and predict the reliability of pre-trained RL agents for real-time congestion management. The approach integrates epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties into a machine learning–based failure prediction model that estimates the probability of RL agent failure one-hour-ahead, accounting for potential contingency scenarios. Results in the Grid2Op environment demonstrate the proposed framework’s ability to anticipate unreliable AI recommendations, achieving an accuracy of 89.5% while maintaining an oversight rate below 7% and a false alarm rate below 11%.

openalex.abstract: Reliable vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is critical for connected and automated driving, where dynamic network topologies, varying traffic densities, and wireless interference can adversely affect latency and stability. While existing learning-based solutions have improved functions such as task offloading and resource allocation, they typically optimize protocol layers in isolation and fail to incorporate safety-oriented control constraints. This paper proposes a cross-layer reinforcement learning framework that jointly performs physical-layer adaptation, medium access control (MAC) congestion control, and edge task offloading. The framework combines constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning with a Lyapunov-based stability mechanism to regulate latency and queue dynamics under time-varying conditions, while a multi-head attention module captures interactions among communication, computation, and vehicular control states. Evaluated in ns-3 under urban and highway scenarios, the proposed approach reduces average end-to-end latency from 13.2 ms to 9.4 ms in the urban scenario and improves packet delivery ratio from 92.1% to 98.3% under the evaluated settings. Furthermore, the safety-aware policy reduces simulated control-instability events and maintains robust communication performance under dynamic traffic conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating cross-layer learning with control-aware safety constraints for reliable V2X communication and edge intelligence.

openalex.abstract: Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) plays a crucial role in supporting latency-sensitive perception tasks in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), thereby improving driving safety and operational efficiency. However, in dense traffic scenarios, heavy contention for MEC computing resources creates two major challenges. First, uncoordinated server selection by vehicles can aggravate network congestion. Second, conventional localized scheduling at Roadside Units (RSUs) may lead to long-term service starvation for some vehicles. Existing task offloading schemes mainly aim to reduce average latency, but often overlook the rejection cost at overloaded nodes and the importance of ensuring long-term service fairness. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a fairness-aware collaborative task offloading and scheduling framework. On the vehicle side, we develop an Adaptive Server Selection for Task Offloading (ASSTO) algorithm, which incorporates rejection penalties into a Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB)-based learning mechanism. This design enables vehicles to autonomously avoid congested RSUs and achieve better load balancing with limited signaling overhead. On the RSU side, we propose an Earliest Virtual Deadline First (EVDF) scheduling algorithm, which replaces fixed physical deadlines with virtual deadlines that reflect both task priority and waiting history, thereby alleviating the starvation of repeatedly deferred requests. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing benchmark schemes by achieving higher task completion rates and better minmax fairness in heterogeneous MEC environments, while still satisfying processing latency requirements.

openalex.abstract: This paper presents a reinforcement learning-based QoS-aware active queue management (AQM) algorithm for congestion control. The presented AQM algorithm monitors the real time queue latency in routers, and calculates the packet dropping or marking probability via a control strategy based on the linear weighted summation of the congestion indicators including instantaneous queuing latency as well as its first- and second-order time derivatives. Instead of adopting the model-driven parameter configuration method as control-theoretic AQM algorithms, a QoS-aware reinforcement learning (RL) agent is elaborately constructed to dynamically tune the control strategy parameters online through policy gradient. By optimizing the QoS-aware objective function, which pursues maximum bandwidth utilization while keeping low queuing latency and jitter by stabling queue latency in bottleneck routers at a low reference level via the AdamW optimizer, the presented AQM system can operate robustly under time varying network conditions. Evaluation results from ns-3 simulations verify that the proposed AQM framework is robust in optimizing core QoS metrics under dynamic network conditions without the need of manual parameter reconfiguration.

openalex.abstract: Real-time communication (RTC) applications require congestion control (CC) mechanisms capable of sustaining high throughput under stringent latency constraints. Although deep reinforcement learning (DRL) provides adaptive control superior to conventional heuristic and loss-based schemes, learned policies often generalize poorly when exposed to unseen network dynamics. To address this limitation without modifying agent architectures or reward formulations, this paper presents GenRL-ACC, a data-centric framework that enhances DRL robustness through generative bandwidth trace augmentation. Using the ReCoCo platform, Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agents are trained across varying synthetic-to-real mixing ratios generated by TTS-GAN and Diffusion-TS, and subsequently evaluated against real-data baselines and Google Congestion Control (GCC) on held-out empirical traces. Experimental results demonstrate that: (1) generative trace augmentation substantially improves downstream Quality of Experience (QoE), where TD3 trained with 50% TTS-GAN traces achieves an 82.65 QoE score-outperforming the real-only baseline by 12.05% and GCC by 8.32%; (2) optimal synthetic-to-real ratios depend fundamentally on the interplay between the generative architecture and the reinforcement learning algorithm; and (3) statistical distribution fidelity alone is insufficient for performance gains, as generative diversity provides a stronger regularizing benefit. Consequently, training data composition must be treated as a co-designed parameter evaluated directly on downstream operational metrics.

openalex.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to decentralized network routing leveraging Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). Traditional reinforcement learning methods often fail to effectively address the complexities of large, dynamic networks, particularly when incorporating communication constraints. This work addresses this limitation by developing an agent-based system where individual routing agents learn optimal routing policies directly within the network topology. The core of the system is a MARL framework that allows agents to coordinate their actions while simultaneously optimizing for key network metrics: throughput and stability. We introduce a specific reward function that explicitly penalizes network congestion and instability, leading to more robust and efficient routing decisions. The proposed method offers a scalable solution for routing in networks with variable communication limitations, representing a significant advancement over centralized approaches and providing a more realistic simulation of real-world network behavior. The presented MARL framework utilizes a Q-learning algorithm, specifically tailored to the multi-agent environment. We evaluate the performance of the system through simulations, demonstrating its ability to achieve high throughput and maintain network stability under diverse operational conditions. The key contributions of this research lie in the design of a MARL agent capable of learning decentralized routing policies considering communication constraints, and the development of a robust reward function to promote stable network operation.

openalex.abstract: Content delivery networks (CDNs) rely on congestion control algorithms (CCAs) to sustain high throughput and low latency. However, existing CCAs are built around single-flow dynamics and do not match modern CDN workloads, where short-lived flows are prevalent on nodes with heterogeneous network conditions and inter-flow competition is intense as one node has to serve hundreds to thousands of concurrent flows. To address this, we propose NLCC, a node-level congestion control framework that configures a set of static CCA parameters shared by flows on a node and regulates the aggregate sending rate of a node. NLCC is composed of three modules. A kernel-aware sensing module exports runtime metrics of flows to the user space. A constraint-aware Bayesian optimization module automatically adapts key CCA parameters for reducing latency, lowering retransmissions, and maintaining throughput. A node-level rate control module caps the node-wise sending rate by deep reinforcement learning for reducing congestion caused by multi-flow competition. We apply NLCC to BBR and evaluate it in CDN production environments. Compared with BBR, NLCC reduces the average retransmission ratio from 16.62% to 11.26% on small nodes and from 3.68% to 2.66% on IDC servers, while maintaining throughput at 1.58/2.12 Gbps versus 1.54/2.08 Gbps for BBR.

openalex.abstract: In datacenter fabrics composed of leaf and aggregation switches, competing flows may become co-located on shared aggregation switches, creating congestion that can significantly degrade protected flows. However, before throughput degradation becomes observable, the network often exhibits early signs characterized by rising flow activity and queue overflow signals. Existing congestion-management approaches primarily react only after congestion becomes visible, leaving these early signs largely unexploited. In this paper, we propose ProFlow, a proactive flow-placement framework for protecting performance-sensitive traffic in multi-tenant datacenter networks, thereby utilizing the early signs of potential throughput degradations. ProFlow leverages distributed telemetry signals and offline-trained reinforcement learning (RL) to identify precursor congestion conditions and proactively reroute protected flows before throughput degradation occurs. Evaluation results using FABRIC testbed show that ProFlow achieves approximately 40% higher mean throughput than a reactive rerouting baseline while initiating rerouting decisions around 34 seconds earlier on average, demonstrating the effectiveness of anticipatory congestion management.

openalex.abstract: Facing price volatility risks and multi-agent strategic interactions in two-level electricity markets, this paper proposes a bi-level decision framework integrating Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) and Mean Field Game (MFG). The upper level minimizes purchasing costs and CVaR risk for inter-provincial traders, while the lower level models market clearing based on generation cost minimization in sending provinces. An MFG model with homogeneous traders is then introduced, coupling individual optimal control (HJB equation) with population distribution evolution (FPK equation) to capture collective behavior feedback on prices. An adaptive regularization Deep Q-Network algorithm is designed to improve computational efficiency. Multi-scenario simulations using grid data analyze the effects of risk aversion, uncertainty, and network congestion on costs and price volatility. Results show that the model effectively characterizes the interplay between risk attitudes and market equilibrium, offering theoretical and practical support for risk management and market design in inter-provincial trading.

openalex.abstract: Abstract Terahertz (THz) and optical wireless communication (OWC) are complementary technologies for sixth-generation (6G) networks, but their practical integration is challenged by severe THz propagation loss and blockage, OWC geometric and field-of-view constraints, mobility, and localization uncertainty. These effects influence not only physical-layer link quality but also Layer~3 (L3) path selection and transport-layer traffic distribution. Existing studies commonly address these functions separately, leaving a gap in reproducible cross-layer frameworks that jointly connect heterogeneous physical states and localization information with L3 path intelligence, multipath transport adaptation, and packet-level network performance. This work proposes a physics-informed (PI) multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) framework with a Multipath TCP (MPTCP)-inspired THz--OWC dual-subflow architecture. The intelligent PI-DDQN--GAT--SAC strategy combines a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) for physics-constrained access and stability decisions, a Graph Attention Network (GAT) for heterogeneous THz--OWC L3 path ranking and selection, and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) for continuous transport-layer subflow allocation. A complementary PI-Static 50/50 strategy provides a deterministic non-learning dual-path reference for persistent parallel utilization. The framework combines Sionna ray-tracing states for the THz--OWC environment, with the OWC branch additionally anchored to calibrated optical-channel parameters, together with localization information. The resulting cross-layer decisions are evaluated through packet-level ns-3/5G-LENA simulations. The results demonstrate coordinated adaptation across the network and transport layers: as THz propagation conditions deteriorate, PI-GAT increasingly favors suitable OWC access paths, while PI-SAC correspondingly shifts a larger fraction of transport traffic toward the OWC subflow. Under the highest evaluated traffic load, PI-DDQN--GAT--SAC improves throughput by approximately 10--12\% over strongest-link selection, which serves as the principal conventional adaptive baseline. THz-only operation is limited by exclusive dependence on the terahertz radio link and its susceptibility to severe blockage and propagation loss, whereas OWC-only operation is constrained by optical geometry, receiver field-of-view, orientation, and blockage. Strongest-link selection adapts between THz and OWC but remains a single-path strategy and therefore cannot exploit simultaneous THz--OWC dual-subflow transmission. PI-Static 50/50 achieves the highest raw parallel capacity when both links remain persistently feasible, revealing a complementary trade-off between fixed dual-path utilization and adaptive L3-aware transport intelligence.

openalex.abstract: An effective method for network congestion avoidance is to optimize the routing. We propose an optimalrouting controlling that combines Deep Reinforcement learning(DRL) based policy optimization andSoftware Defined Network(SDN) based flow control. It uses DRL to learn the optimal network routingpolicy in different traffic patterns. SDN controller provides network traffic information for DRL agent tomake decision, and implements flow routing control according to the decision. The results of simulationexperiments show that our DRL-based route optimization has good performances in congestionavoidance.

openalex.display_name: "Training Performance Dataset for SAC-APF-EE Compared with Other SOTA Algorithms"
openalex.abstract: "This dataset provides training performance and end-effector motion trajectory data for the comparative evaluation of SAC-APF-EE and related methods. It comprises 16 Excel workbooks organized into four categories: reward convergence, training stability, training success rate, and end motion trajectories. The training performance data cover SAC-APF-EE, SAC-M, TD3-M, and DDPG-M, with results for five random seeds over 500 training episodes per method. Reward records include individual seed values, aggregate statistics, and Gaussian-smoothed mean rewards. Training stability and success rate summaries are provided for five consecutive 100-episode intervals. The motion trajectory data contain three-dimensional tool center point (TCP) positions for SAC-APF-EE, APF-M, Bi-RRT-M, and FAPP-A. All trajectory coordinates are expressed in the robot base coordinate frame. This dataset supports the reconstruction of training performance plots and three-dimensional end-effector paths, comparative analysis of learning behavior and trajectory geometry, and examination of variability across random seeds."

openalex.abstract: In environments with large movable obstacles, detour-only navigation can be inefficient or even infeasible, while obstacle interaction requires reasoning about navigation benefit, feasible placement, and executable manipulation. We present a hierarchical navigation among movable obstacles (NAMO) framework for mobile manipulators. At the high level, the planner identifies key blocking obstacles from reference paths and searches for relocation plans that jointly satisfy geometric, manipulation, and downstream navigation constraints. When direct relocation is hindered by other movable objects, a large language model (LLM) is selectively invoked to infer auxiliary manipulation dependencies, which are then verified by deterministic geometric planning. To execute the resulting relocation goals, we define discrete contact modes on the surfaces of box-shaped obstacles and select contact faces and regions online based on position and orientation errors, enabling straight, side, and corner pushing through contact switching. A recurrent reinforcement-learning policy coordinates the mobile base and manipulator to track tool center point (TCP) targets while preserving end-effector reachability during sustained pushing. Simulation and real-robot experiments demonstrate feasible navigation-manipulation in detour, single- and multi-obstacle relocation, and dependency-constrained scenarios, validating the framework for interactive navigation with large non-graspable obstacles. The open-source project is available at https://cloudytosunny.github.io/NAMO_DCPushing/.

openalex.abstract: Introduction While blockchain integration within Electronic Healthcare Record (EHR) platforms has strengthened data integrity and patient privacy, practical deployment continues to suffer from elevated latency and inflexible processing mechanisms. This work presents the AI-Accelerated Blockchain Architecture (AIBA-EHR), a framework engineered to accelerate transaction processing and enable adaptive security measures suitable for real-world clinical environments. Methods Our approach couples a lightweight Python-based blockchain implementation with asynchronous parallel block validation and machine-learning-driven consensus parameter optimization. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning agent anticipates network congestion and dynamically calibrates block size alongside validation difficulty. A risk estimation module built on Temporal Convolutional Networks with Attention Mechanisms (TCN + AM) prioritizes trustworthy nodes and identifies anomalous access behavior. The TCN + AM module employs dilated causal convolutions with dilation rates d ∈ {1,2,4,8}, yielding a receptive field of 31 time steps that fully covers the 20-step access sequences used in this study. Results Experimental evaluation using synthetic EHR datasets comprising 120,000 access events across 15 features reveals a mean confirmation latency of 25.7 s and an average throughput of 209.7 transactions per second (TPS), representing a 40% reduction in confirmation latency and a 25% improvement in throughput relative to fixed-parameter blockchain baselines. The TCN + AM anomaly detector achieves an F1-score of 0.9942, precision of 0.9953, recall of 0.9931, and AUC of 0.9950 across five-fold cross-validation (mean ± std: 0.9935 ± 0.0018), outperforming all sequential and tabular baselines on classification metrics. Discussion These findings indicate that the strategic fusion of artificial intelligence with distributed ledger technology can simultaneously achieve operational efficiency and robust security, enabling real-time healthcare data exchange without compromising patient privacy across decentralized infrastructures.

openalex.abstract: Abstract Wireless body area networks (WBANs) are widely used in both medical and non-medical applications. In these networks, routing protocols face specific challenges due to energy constraints, bandwidth limitations, heterogeneity, node mobility, and dynamic topology. Although reinforcement learning (RL), particularly Q-learning, can improve routing performance in WBANs, existing Q-learning-based approaches often suffer from large state spaces, slow convergence, fixed learning parameters, inefficient topology management, and limited capability to recover routing failures. This study proposes a Q-learning-based mobility-aware tree routing protocol (QMTR) for WBANs integrated with vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) to support reliable transmission of passengers’ health data to remote medical centers. QMTR employs a two-stage screening mechanism to reduce the learning space. The first screening stage retains only neighboring nodes that provide geographical progress toward the destination, whereas the second stage eliminates routing candidates that may violate the tree structure. Furthermore, the learning rate is dynamically adjusted according to a comprehensive link-quality index consisting of link lifetime, link delay, and link stability. The protocol further incorporates an adaptive hello-message interval to balance topology accuracy and routing overhead, and a recovery mechanism that temporarily relaxes routing constraints to reconnect isolated nodes without restarting the learning process. Extensive simulations are conducted using Network Simulator 3 (NS3) to evaluate QMTR against existing routing schemes, including ARMR, VehiHealth, and GPSR, under varying vehicle speeds and packet-sending rates. In the first simulation scenario, the evaluation outcomes show that QMTR improves packet delivery rate (PDR) and network lifespan by 3.58% and 8.38%, respectively, and reduces end-to-end delay (EED) by 28.15%. Although QMTR introduces approximately 9.57% higher routing overhead than ARMR in this scenario, it achieves better reliability and energy efficiency. In the second simulation scenario, QMTR increases PDR and network lifespan by 3.73% and 6.48%, respectively, and decreases EED and RO by 21.92% and 13.70%, respectively.

openalex.abstract: Patients with chronic diseases alternate between stable conditions and high-risk episodes that require continuous and accurate monitoring. Telemedicine systems rely on multiple battery-powered personal devices to collect and transmit health data over wireless networks, allowing clinicians to access updated patient information, especially in critical situations. However, frequent data collection and transmission can shorten device battery life, while an increasing number of monitored patients may cause network congestion and higher communication latency. To address these challenges, this thesis proposes an edge-computing solution that dynamically adjusts data collection and transmission frequency according to each patient's condition. A reinforcement learning algorithm based on a discrete Soft Actor-Critic policy is used to prioritize patients: critical patients are monitored and their data transmitted immediately to ensure low latency, while stable patients are monitored less frequently, reducing network traffic and extending battery lifetime.

openalex.abstract: Fog–cloud systems allow distributed and latency-sensitive IoT applications to share edge, fog, and cloud resources for efficient computation, storing and delivering services. Nonetheless, the current methods of task scheduling and resource allocation tend to be based on deterministic prediction, heuristic schedules, or response optimization, restricting risk sensitivity and responsiveness to dynamic workloads. To address these issues, we propose a graph network with a reinforcement learning framework to avoid congestion and schedule tasks with a low makespan in fog–IoT systems. The work starts with real-time monitoring of queue states, delay, bandwidth, energy and deadline properties of upcoming IoT tasks. Quantile Regression Long Short-Term Memory (QR-LSTM) predicts a normal task flow and congestion based on the task queue. The congestion tasks are further scheduled using a Delay-Aware Influence Reinforced-Graph Neural Network (DAIR-GNN). Then, Topology-Sensitive Resource Influence Propagation is used to map and analyze the relationship between the task sender and receiver within a network. After that, Dual-Stage Risk-Aware Hierarchical Policy (DRHP) combines Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to select the kinds of sources, like fog or cloud, based on the topology. Similarly, Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) with Soft Actor–Critic allocates the resources of each tasks within the selected server. Both RL models are trained using Few-Shot Adaptive Policy Transfer to make better predictions. Lastly, Confidence-Uncertainty Regulated Exploration (CURE) is used to compute the prediction score for task allocation improvement. The proposed framework achieves a variance ratio of 80.6%, latency is 0.626 s, and the success rate is 98% in the prediction of congestion, scheduling and allocation of resources. These results demonstrate the improved ability to ensure reliable and effective fog–cloud allocation in response to dynamically changing workloads.

openalex.abstract: The fast growing domain of Internet of Things (IoT) applications leads to significant pressure on wireless sensor networks. Consequently, congestion and packet delivery delays are considered inherent characteristics of resource-constrained devices. Conducting a literature review, this paper summarizes the latest developments on fuzzy logic, reinforcement learning, and hybrid lightweight models for Adaptive Congestion Control (ACC) and analyzes their effectiveness in improving network reliability, delay, energy efficiency and overall network performance metrics. While many studies describe encouraging enhancements, the field remains challenged by issues related to computational cost, limited scalability verification, and a lack of real-world experimental validation. These observations emphasize the demand for computationally light, interpretable, and scalable adaptive frameworks with real-time responsiveness in heterogeneous IoT environments. The paper also outlines future research directions toward designing sustainable and reliable congestion-control solutions for upcoming IoT systems.

openalex.abstract: Robotic contact-rich and fine-grained manipulation remains a significant challenge due to complex interaction dynamics and the competing requirements of multi-timescale control. While current visual imitation learning methods excel at long-horizon planning, they often fail to perceive critical interaction cues like friction variations or incipient slip, and struggle to balance global task coherence with local reactive feedback. To address these challenges, we propose M2-ResiPolicy, a novel Master-Micro residual control architecture that synergizes high-level action guidance with low-level correction. The framework consists of a Master-Guidance Policy (MGP) operating at 10 Hz, which generates temporally consistent action chunks via a diffusion-based backbone and employs a tactile-intensity-driven adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically modulate perceptual weights between vision and touch. Simultaneously, a high-frequency (60 Hz) Micro-Residual Corrector (MRC) utilizes a lightweight GRU to provide real-time action compensation based on TCP wrench feedback. This policy is further integrated with a force-mixed PBIC execution layer, effectively regulating contact forces to ensure interaction safety. Experiments across several demanding tasks including fragile object grasping and precision insertion, demonstrate that M2-ResiPolicy significantly outperforms standard Diffusion Policy (DP) and state-of-the-art Reactive Diffusion Policy (RDP), achieving a 93\% damage-free success rate in chip grasping and superior force regulation stability.

openalex.abstract: Large-scale distributed artificial intelligence (AI) workloads couple congestion across sources, destinations, and parallel paths, while traffic bursts and recovery change network conditions over time. Reliable remote direct memory access (RDMA) routing therefore requires distributed, history-aware telemetry and must respect packet-order and switch-resource constraints. We present DERIR ( DPU-Empowered Reliable and Intelligent Routing ), a DPU–switch co-designed multipath routing framework that fuses spatio-temporal network state. Endpoint DPUs arrange current and recent flow statistics in a source–destination matrix and use multi-agent deep reinforcement learning to select flows with the largest expected system-wide benefit. Source top-of-rack switches combine current local queue delay with smoothed one-byte downstream feedback. Destination switches repair bounded packet reordering before RDMA network interface card (RNIC) delivery. We implement DERIR on NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPUs and Spectrum-4 programmable switches and evaluate it on a 4-ary 100-Gbps RDMA over Converged Ethernet version 2 (RoCEv2) Fat-tree testbed. On this testbed, DERIR reduces average flow completion time (FCT) by at least 23.85% and P99.99 FCT by more than 21.8%. It also improves effective bandwidth utilization by 9.3%–14%. These results show that selective routing based on distributed state can exploit path diversity while bounding forwarding, buffering, and reordering costs.

openalex.abstract: In order to address the challenges of making the multi-dimensional value of flexibility resources explicit in high-proportion renewable energy power systems, as well as the difficulty of traditional scheduling methods in coping with the uncertainty of both generation and load sides, this paper proposes a closed-loop scheduling framework of "Value Quantification-Robust Optimization-Intelligent Coordination". A multi-dimensional resource value assessment model embedded with Conditional Value at Risk is developed to quantify the reliability, congestion management, environmental, and regulation values, along with the design of a "value flow" tracking algorithm. Furthermore, a value-driven distributional robust optimization model is established, integrating the value signal into the day-ahead scheduling objectives. A real-time collaborative decision-making mechanism based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning is designed to achieve dynamic optimization at both intra-day and real-time scales. Simulations based on actual grid data show that the proposed VD-MA strategy reduces the total system operation cost by an average of 12.7%, 8.3%, and 5.1% compared to deterministic optimization, two-stage stochastic optimization, and traditional robust optimization, respectively. The curtailment rate of renewable energy decreases by 9.4%, 6.8%, and 4.2%, respectively. In extreme scenarios, it can reduce the net load fluctuation during the midday sharp drop of photovoltaic power by approximately 35%. Value analysis further reveals that, in a scenario with 70% high penetration, the collaboration between demand-side response and gas turbines reduces the reserve cost by 24.5%, and the environmental value of energy storage can increase by 6.2 times as carbon prices rise. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively unleashes the potential of flexibility resources, offering significant advantages in improving economic efficiency, security, and low-carbon performance.

openalex.display_name: Machine Learning-Driven Interoperability for Cross-Chain Provenance: A Computationally Validated Trust Layer for Global Artisanal Sourcing
openalex.abstract: Overview This project presents the architectural design, conceptual framework, and initial computational validation of an omnichannel marketplace platform that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and blockchain technologies to address systemic challenges in the global artisanal goods market. The core problems addressed are the lack of verifiable product authenticity and provenance, information asymmetry between artisans and buyers, limited market access for independent creators (especially in developing regions), and the vulnerability of blockchain systems to “first-mile fraud” (where non-authentic goods are entered onto the ledger before cryptographic recording begins). The platform combines three synergistic components: 1. An AI-powered recommendation engine informed by neuroaesthetics and neuromarketing principles to optimize product discovery, artistic presentation, and emotional resonance. 2. A blockchain-based provenance tracking system using Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) for immutable, verifiable records of authenticity and ownership. 3. A Machine Learning-Driven Interoperability layer that secures and optimizes cross-chain asset transfers, enabling scalable, high-security movement of provenance data and NFTs across disparate blockchain networks. Purpose The primary purpose is to establish a computationally validated trust layer for transparent and sustainable artisanal commerce. By synthesizing existing quantitative evidence and performing simulation-based validation, the work aims to define performance benchmarks for AI recommendation systems, blockchain/NFT provenance mechanisms, and ML-enhanced cross-chain interoperability. These benchmarks guide the platform’s design so that technical assurance (immutable records and secure transfers) translates into cognitive and emotional confidence for buyers, while simultaneously empowering artisans through data sovereignty and Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) governance. Methodology (as implemented) The completed study followed a systematic review with meta-analysis design. A curated corpus of 41 scholarly articles (selected via purposive sampling) covering blockchain, machine learning, computational design, neuromarketing, and related domains served as the knowledge base. Quantitative evidence was synthesized to estimate effect sizes and performance improvements related to: - AI recommendation systems and their impact on e-commerce conversion rates and perceived personalization; - Blockchain/NFT implementations and their effects on transparency, trust, and authenticity verification; - Machine Learning applications to blockchain interoperability (anomaly detection, data integrity validation, and route optimization). A computational simulation was then conducted using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to model predictive route optimization under varying network congestion conditions. Additional algorithmic approaches (Random Forests for integrity validation and Graph Neural Networks for multi-chain relationship mapping) were specified as part of the interoperability layer. Weighting factors in a multi-objective cost function for route selection were optimized via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning in simulated high-congestion environments. Key Expected / Synthesized Outcomes From the meta-analytic synthesis and simulation: - AI recommendation engine (neuroaesthetically informed): expected +15% conversion rate lift (Hedges’ g = 0.45) relative to non-personalized systems. - ML-Driven Interoperability layer: average 18% reduction in cross-chain transaction latency (validated simulation range 0.8–1.2 seconds versus baseline 1.0–1.5 seconds). - ML anomaly detection and integrity validation: projected ~25% reduction in fraud/counterfeit risk. - NFT provenance system: increased user-perceived trust (supported by existing blockchain literature). These benchmarks support the feasibility of achieving Sustainable Artisanal Commerce through a cognitively optimized digital marketplace. Future empirical phases (outlined but not executed in this study) include small-scale pilot testing with artisans and psychophysiological measures (eye-tracking, heart-rate variability) to quantify emotional resonance and cognitive certainty. Status and Transparency Note This registration is retrospective. The meta-analytic synthesis, computational simulation, and conceptual framework described above had already been completed at the time of registration. The purpose of this OSF record is to provide a permanent, timestamped, citable description of the methods and synthesized findings for transparency and reproducibility. Keywords Blockchain; Machine Learning; Cross-Chain Interoperability; NFT Provenance; Neuroaesthetics; Neuromarketing; Artisanal Commerce; Trust Layer; Meta-Analysis.

openalex.abstract: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) are increasingly used in resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) environments, yet their robustness is often evaluated against static attacks rather than adversaries that adapt to detection feedback. This paper investigates adaptive port-scan evasion against ML-based IDS models deployed on a Raspberry Pi 3B+. We implement a live Zeek-based IDS pipeline with XGBoost, a multi-layer perceptron, and a 1D convolutional neural network trained on TON_IoT telemetry, and use a Deep Q-Network (DQN) adversary to learn evasive combinations of probe timing, TCP flags, and payload size under black-box, gray-box, and white-box feature-visibility settings. Although the deployed IDS models detect conventional port scans at 91.1--99.8%, DQN final-50-episode evasion rates range from 61.9% to 98.3% across feature-visibility settings. Greater feature visibility does not monotonically improve evasion, and its effect is model-dependent: against XGBoost, the black-box agent achieves 92.9% evasion, compared with 61.9% and 76.9% for gray-box and white-box agents, respectively, whereas 1D-CNN is most vulnerable under white-box access at 98.1%. Because standard DQN can overestimate action values, we additionally spot-check representative conditions using Double DQN. The gray-box condition remains unstable in this check, providing no evidence that overestimation bias alone explains the observed instability. These results show that limited feature knowledge can still enable effective adaptive evasion against static edge-deployed IDS models, motivating more robust defenses for IoT edge environments.
